title: Generalized Mirror Theory Conjecture
statement_paraphrase: That the count of non-degenerate solutions to a cycle-consistent bivariate XOR system on an arbitrary multi-graph obeys the falling-factorial lower bound whenever q and the maximum component size are both o(sqrt(N)), i.e. with the known assumption q*xi^2 << N relaxed to q*xi = o(N).

queries_run: mirror theory xi_max range Cogliati Dutta Nandi Patarin Seurin component size
proof of mirror theory wide range

evidence.claim: The best published result proves the P_i xor P_j theorem for xi_max up to O(2^{n/4}/sqrt n) under the assumption q*xi_max^2 << 2^n, via a new 'link-deletion equation'; the paper states Patarin's original general-xi_max proof has non-trivial gaps.
evidence.citation: Cogliati, Dutta, Nandi, Patarin, Saha, Proof of Mirror Theory for a Wide Range of xi_max, EUROCRYPT 2023

evidence.claim: No source found proving the o(sqrt N) / linear-in-xi_max form for arbitrary multi-graphs. Neighbouring 2024-25 work (Mind the Bad Norms; Toward Full n-bit Security) refines applications rather than the mirror bound itself; not read in full.
Patarin (2003, 2005) and Cogliati-Seurin (2018, circle graphs, xi_max = O(N^{1/3})) fix the earlier rungs as transcribed on the page.
evidence.citation: Patarin CRYPTO 2003; Cogliati and Seurin, DCC 2018

P1.justification: A counting lower bound with no adversary at all. The proof side is an inequality on h(G,lambda); the machine-friendly side is the refutation, an explicit (G,lambda) whose exact solution count falls below the bound, computable by integer enumeration at n=3,4. Two-sided in the weak sense that the constructive side is a counterexample rather than partial credit.
P1.construction_side_dual: An explicit cycle-consistent (G, lambda) with q, xi_max within the hypothesis whose exact non-degenerate solution count h(G,lambda) is strictly below (N)_q/N^m times the claimed error factor; exhaustively enumerable for N=8,16 and q<=6.

P2.justification: The restriction axis is the exponent on xi_max in the admissibility assumption: settled at q*xi_max^2 << N (EUROCRYPT 2023), target q*xi_max = o(N). Intermediate rungs (exponent 1.5) are well defined and unsettled, the link-deletion recursion is the feature expected to survive, and the gap is two rungs. Monotone: a weaker assumption is strictly harder.
P2.restriction_axis: exponent e in the admissibility assumption q*xi_max^e << N (settled e=2, target e=1)
P2.settled_base_case: e=2, arbitrary forests, xi_max <= O(N^{1/4}/sqrt n), Cogliati-Dutta-Nandi-Patarin-Saha
P2.next_rung: e=1.5 for forests, i.e. q*xi_max^{1.5} << N
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The link-deletion recursion over component size survives verbatim; only the accounting of higher-order dependency intersections has to be re-done, since the recursion itself never used e=2.

P3.justification: Capped. The page names two obstructions that are new machinery, not new accounting: explicit structural cancellation lemmas for higher-order dependency intersections, and tight lower bounds for exact character sums over non-abelian representations. Composition depth 2 (Patarin's framework plus the 2023 link-deletion proof), and the ambient convention load is heavy: non-degeneracy, cycle consistency, the xi_max counting convention and the unstated admissibility side conditions all come from the sources' preliminaries.
P3.candidate_technique: mirror theory / link-deletion equations, with H-coefficient accounting; character sums as the fallback

V1.justification: Loses on single-reading and on pinned asymptotics. The conjecture is stated for arbitrary multi-graphs but the 'equivalently' restatement covers only tree components, so it is unclear whether the same formula is asserted at circuit rank > 0; and 'q <= o(N^{1/2})' plus an unquantified O(.) inside the conclusion leave the asymptotic conventions unpinned. Wins on: standard model with no idealization, no adversary to specify, composition explicitly not applicable, and a nameable vacuous reading.
V1.idealization: standard model, pure combinatorics over F_2^n
variants_in_play: forests / trees only
arbitrary multi-graphs at circuit rank > 0
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove it only where q*xi_max = Omega(N), so the factor (1 - O(q*xi_max/N)) is non-positive and the bound is trivially true, or only for forests at e=2 where it is already a theorem.

V2.justification: Maximal, and the reason to buy a Refuter here. For n=3,4 (N=8,16) and q<=6 the whole space of cycle-consistent labelled multi-graphs is enumerable and h(G,lambda) is an exact integer count, so the claim is decidable by exhaustive rational arithmetic; the predicate hardens with integer-only arithmetic plus an admissibility check that raises on cycle-inconsistent or disconnected input; and there is a scalar to minimise.
V2.finite_instantiation: n in {3,4}, q <= 6, all cycle-consistent labellings, exact integer solution counting

V3.justification: Lean plus Mathlib is a genuine match: finite counting over F_2^n with no oracle measure theory and no asymptotics inside the object. But the lemma-level decomposition at the new rungs is the research content, so the human-supplied decomposition is not cheap. An exact small-case computation is a real machine-checkable witness short of a proof.

O1.justification: The worst case for the obscurity dividend. Mirror Theory is a named conjecture with a twenty-year tradition running through Patarin 2003 and 2005, and the papers that cite it as open also attempt it: Cogliati-Seurin 2018, Cogliati-Dutta-Nandi-Patarin-Saha 2023, Dutta-Nandi on xi_max=2, and the 2024-25 applications line. High attention, no recency dividend.

O2.justification: Sources are all reachable (CRYPTO 2003 via the IACR archive, DCC 2018 via the author page, ePrint 2022/686) and the compute profile is bounded. But mirror theory proofs are paper-length developments with no natural short lemma chain: ePrint 2022/686 runs tens of pages, and the error accounting is not separable into independently statable pieces.

reasons: R1: pre-cutoff sources in a heavily worked area, so recall can supply the settled rungs and a produced argument has to be re-scouted on technique rather than on statement

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $q \cdot \xi_{\max}^{3/2} \ll N$ for arbitrary forest graphs, i.e. the EUROCRYPT 2023 statement with the exponent on $\xi_{\max}$ lowered from $2$ to $3/2$
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Exhaustive exact enumeration at $N=8,16$, $q \le 6$ over all cycle-consistent labelled forests: either exhibit an instance violating the claimed factor, or certify the minimum of $h(G,\lambda) N^m / (N)_q$ over the enumerated space, which pins how much slack the conjectured error term actually has.
configuration.yield_on_failure: A table of the exact worst-case slack at small $N$, which tells the Case Planner whether the linear-in-$\xi_{\max}$ error term is even the right shape before any Prover budget is spent.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: whether circuit rank > 0 is in scope, or the statement is forests-only
the intended quantifier on the O(.) inside the conclusion

source_requests.what_is_needed: The exact statement of the admissibility assumption and the link-deletion equation, and where e=2 is used.
source_requests.step_that_collapses_without_it: The entry rung is defined by lowering that exponent; without the exact assumption there is no rung.

title: Tight Time-Space Tradeoffs for k-Collisions with Auxiliary Input
statement_paraphrase: That in the auxiliary-input random oracle model any adversary with S bits of advice and T online queries that finds a k-collision in an unsalted random oracle H:[N]->[N] with probability at least 1/2 must satisfy S^{k-1} T^k = Omega(N^{k-1}).

queries_run: time-space tradeoff multicollision auxiliary input salted random oracle k-collision lower bound
Akshima multi-collision Merkle-Damgard auxiliary input

evidence.claim: The k-way analogue that is actually studied is SALTED and Merkle-Damgard: 'the best known attack for finding B-blocks m-way collision ... when m^{1/(B-1)}-way collisions exist on every salt', with advantage forms like Otilde(S/mN) and Otilde(STB/N), and optimality shown only at B=1 and B=2. Nothing of the form S^{k-1}T^k = N^{k-1} appears.
evidence.citation: Akshima, Time-Space Tradeoffs for Finding Multi-Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hash Functions, ITC 2024

evidence.claim: The k=2 baseline the page transcribes as S*T^2 = Theta(N) is the salted collision-resistance statement, not an unsalted one; the whole AI-ROM collision line (Coretti-Dodis-Guo-Steinberger, Akshima-Cash-Drucker-Wee, Akshima-Guo-Liu) is stated relative to a random salt.
evidence.citation: Coretti, Dodis, Guo, Steinberger, Random Oracles and Non-Uniformity, EUROCRYPT 2018; Akshima, Cash, Drucker, Wee, CRYPTO 2020

evidence.claim: The unsalted statement as written on the page is refuted in one line: a random H:[N]->[N] has about N/6 3-collisions, so A_1 stores one in 3 log N bits and A_2 outputs it with T=0, giving success probability 1-o(1) while S^2 T^3 = 0. The same argument kills every k >= 2.

definitions_needing_repair: No salt. The online stage receives no challenge, so the advice can simply contain a k-collision and win with T=0; a salt (or a keyed/Merkle-Damgard chaining input drawn after the advice is fixed) has to be added before the statement is non-vacuous.

Threshold versus advantage. The page fixes epsilon >= 1/2 and asserts a threshold on S^{k-1}T^k; the literature it cites bounds the ADVANTAGE as a function of S, T and N. The two are not interchangeable at the k=2 baseline it quotes.

Block length. The k=2 result quoted as tight is tight for salted collisions; the multicollision results are indexed by the block bound B, which the page does not mention at all, and B is exactly what the known m-way bounds depend on.

P1.justification: Scored for the record only; the gate stops the campaign. A time-space lower bound against an adversary with unbounded offline access and S bits of advice, which is the least machine-friendly direction; the attack side is a construction and is where the trivial refutation lives.
P1.construction_side_dual: The one-line advice attack: A_1 stores a single k-collision of H in k log N bits, A_2 outputs it with no online query. This is what refutes the statement as written, and any repaired statement must exclude it.

P2.justification: The axis (k) has a settled base case at k=2, but only in the salted model the page has dropped, so the base case does not sit on the same ladder as the target. The next rung (k=3) is well defined once salting is restored.
P2.restriction_axis: collision multiplicity k
P2.settled_base_case: k=2, salted, ST^2 = Theta(N)
P2.next_rung: k=3, salted, B=1 or B=2
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The compression / high-knowledge-gaining event structure of the k=2 argument survives; the counting over pre-image hypergraphs is what changes.

P3.justification: Capped. The page's own diagnosis is that compression and bit-fixing 'fail to capture the multi-way combinatorial synergy', and the ITC 2024 work reaches optimality only at B=1,2 with a bespoke argument. Composition depth 3 or more (CDGS presampling, ACDW/AGL compression, the ITC 2024 multicollision counting).
P3.candidate_technique: compression and presampling; high-knowledge-gaining event decomposition

V1.justification: This is where the record fails, and it is the heaviest-weighted axis for exactly this reason. There is no salt, so the adversary class and the winning condition together admit a trivial win; the epsilon >= 1/2 threshold form does not match the advantage form of every result cited; and the k=2 entry in the page's own comparison table is a salted theorem transcribed without its salt. Wins only on: the idealization is named unambiguously (AI-ROM), and a vacuous reading is easy to state.
V1.idealization: AI-ROM (auxiliary-input random oracle), unsalted
variants_in_play: unsalted AI-ROM (as written)
salted AI-ROM (the literature)
Merkle-Damgard with B-block bound (the multicollision literature)
V1.vacuous_reading: Store a k-collision in the advice and answer with zero online queries: success probability 1-o(1) with S = k log N and T = 0, so the claimed inequality fails and the statement is false as written rather than open.

V2.justification: The refutation is not merely finite, it is closed-form, and a small exact computation confirms it: for n <= 12 enumerate a random H:[N]->[N], count k-collisions exactly, and verify that one exists with probability 1-o(1) while k log N << N^{(k-1)/k}. Exact integer arithmetic throughout; the scalar is the advice length needed.
V2.finite_instantiation: n in {8,...,12}, exact k-collision census over sampled H, k in {3,4}

V3.justification: A counterexample certificate exists and is trivial to check. No tool match for the repaired statement: AI-ROM lower bounds need measure-theoretic probability over oracle spaces plus asymptotics, which is thinly covered in every assistant listed, and the lemma decomposition for the k>=3 counting is the research content.

O1.justification: Provenance is a stated conjecture, not an aside, and the area is active: Akshima, Cash, Drucker, Wee, Guo, Liu, Ghoshal, Komargodski, Freitag all work it, and the ITC 2024 paper attempts exactly the multicollision cell. The one point is for the narrowness of the k>=3 sub-cell, which has a single paper on it.

O2.justification: Sources reachable (ITC 2024 open access, CDGS EUROCRYPT 2018, ACDW CRYPTO 2020, Hellman 1980) and compute bounded, but a k>=3 AI-ROM lower bound is a paper-length development; the ITC 2024 optimality proofs at B=1,2 are not short.

reasons: R1: pre-cutoff, well-studied area; a produced 'proof' is at high risk of being a recalled salted theorem re-labelled, which is precisely the mistranscription the gate is firing on

source_requests.citation: Akshima, Time-Space Tradeoffs for Finding Multi-Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hash Functions, ITC 2024
source_requests.what_is_needed: The exact salted m-way statements and which (m,B) cells are proved optimal.
source_requests.step_that_collapses_without_it: The repaired conjecture's target regime cannot be named, and the repaired statement may already be a theorem.

source_requests.citation: Coretti, Dodis, Guo, Steinberger, Random Oracles and Non-Uniformity, EUROCRYPT 2018
source_requests.what_is_needed: The exact form of the k=2 salted collision bound the page quotes as ST^2 = Theta(N).
source_requests.step_that_collapses_without_it: The base case of the ladder is not the statement the page attributes to it.

title: No Two-Element Split NILPs (the information-theoretic core of Groth16 optimality)
statement_paraphrase: That no split non-interactive linear proof with proof dimension k1 = k2 = 1 and completeness error at most 1 - 1/poly can be statistically sound against affine prover strategies for a relation generator with hard decisional problems.

queries_run: pairing-based SNARG two group elements Arnon Dujmovic Yogev pure generic group model
Groth16 proof size optimality open problem

evidence.claim: Arnon, Dujmovic and Yogev do construct a two-group-element pairing-based SNARG, but in GGM+ROM (Maurer plus an oracle from group elements to bits), using the oracle to derive the verifier's otherwise-unpredictable query, with imperfect completeness. The pure-GGM two-element question is their own first open problem.
evidence.citation: Arnon, Dujmovic, Yogev, Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements, ePrint 2025/2160
evidence.eprint_version_date: revised 2026-02-12, per the page's own bibliography

evidence.claim: Groth poses the two-element question as the closing open problem of the paper that gives the three-element scheme; his Theorems 3-4 rule out one element in the split-NILP model.
evidence.citation: Groth, On the Size of Pairing-Based Non-Interactive Arguments, EUROCRYPT 2016

evidence.claim: No source found closing the (1,1) cell in either direction. Neighbouring 2025 work (Designated-verifier SNARGs with one group element, CRYPTO 2025) moves a different restriction.
rungs_tried: the page's own bibliography, checked for a later revision

P1.justification: Genuinely two-sided with a machine-friendly constructive side. The proof direction is an impossibility over all candidates, but the object being quantified over is finite-dimensional algebra: proof matrices Pi_1, Pi_2 in F^{1 x m_j} and test matrices T_i over a field. Refuting it means exhibiting one (1,1) split NILP, which is a search over small matrices with an exactly computable soundness error.
P1.construction_side_dual: A split NILP with k1 = k2 = 1 for an NP-complete relation: proof matrices Pi_1, Pi_2 and tests T_1..T_eta over F_p such that honest proofs verify with probability at least 1/poly and no affine prover strategy forges except with negligible probability over sigma. Searchable exhaustively at p in {5,7,11}, m_1, m_2 <= 4, eta <= 3.

P2.justification: One clean rung with a fully settled base case (one element, impossible: Gro16 Thms 3-4, extended by ADY25 to arbitrary Maurer-generic verifiers under OWFs), and a well-defined unsettled next rung (k1 = k2 = 1). The generalization hypothesis is statable and the page states it: the yes-instance sampling attack is the surviving feature. Minus one because the base case is a special-case accident in exactly the sense the rubric warns about: the one-element bound runs on uniqueness, and the page records that at (1,1) the sampling attack 'no longer isolates' the accepting value, so the base-case mechanism provably fails one rung up.
P2.restriction_axis: proof dimension (k1, k2), equivalently the number of source-group elements
P2.settled_base_case: (1,0) and (0,1), one group element: impossible for hard relation generators
P2.next_rung: (1,1), two elements, one per source group
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The yes-instance sampling attack survives; what changes is that it must isolate a Mobius curve of accepting pairs (A,B) rather than a single accepting value, since every verification term is affine in the prover's coefficients except the single bilinear monomial AB.

P3.justification: Capped, and the cap is the honest call. The page's own Remark 1 says the sampling attacks behind Gro16 Thms 3-4 and the ADY25 one-element bound 'die on exactly that monomial', so the (1,1) case needs a new mechanism rather than a re-run of the old one; the repo grades it new-idea for the same reason. Composition depth 2 (Gro16 plus ADY25) and a heavy ambient load: split-NILP syntax, affine prover strategies, the purist model and 'hard decisional problems' are all Gro16 preliminaries the statement silently depends on.
P3.candidate_technique: explicit adversary construction: yes-instance sampling against the Mobius curve of accepting (A,B) pairs; alternatively a Valiant-Vazirani-style unique-witness transfer, which the page records only as a half-remembered lead

V1.justification: Loses only on single-reading, and for a structural reason: the LaTeX source of c/0008 and c/0009 is byte-identical and states both conjectures, so nothing in the statement document fixes which one this record is about. Only index.qmd does. Everything else is pinned: Maurer's GGM explicitly and 'no random oracle, no channel from group elements to bits' explicitly; the affine prover class fully specified as unbounded and sigma-independent; completeness error and decisional hardness quantified; composition not applicable; and a vacuous reading is easy to name.
V1.idealization: pure generic bilinear group model, Maurer's formulation, no auxiliary oracles
variants_in_play: pure GGM (Maurer), the subject
GGM+ROM, where two elements are achieved by ADY25
Type I / symmetric groups, where two elements suffice
the split-NILP core (this record) versus the compiled purist argument (c/0009)
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove nonexistence only for PERFECTLY complete (1,1) split NILPs, which is close to what Gro16's dimension count already gives, and which the 'completeness error at most 1 - 1/poly' clause exists precisely to exclude.

V2.justification: The strongest refutation affordance in this part of the corpus. Fix F_p with p small, m_1, m_2 <= 4, k1 = k2 = 1, eta <= 3 and a toy relation with an explicit Yes/No sampler; then completeness and the affine-prover forging probability are both exact rational quantities computable by enumeration over sigma, so the (1,1) cell is decidable at those parameters. Exact arithmetic over F_p hardens the predicate, and admissibility checks (sigma contains 1, the relation is non-trivial, eta >= 1) rule out the degenerate wins.
V2.finite_instantiation: F_p for p in {5,7,11}; m_1, m_2 <= 4; eta <= 3; toy relation with explicit Yes/No samplers; exhaustive over Test and ProofMatrix families

V3.justification: Lean plus Mathlib genuinely fits: the object is finite-field linear and bilinear algebra with no oracle measure theory and no asymptotics inside the core claim. The decomposition is not cheap, because the case analysis on the structure of the test matrices is the research content. A counterexample certificate (an explicit (1,1) NILP with its exact soundness error) is a real machine-checkable witness.

O1.justification: Not an aside: Groth states it himself, and ADY25 restates it as their first open problem. But attention as an OPEN PROBLEM is genuinely low, as distinct from the enormous citation count of Groth16 itself: the follow-ups (ADY25, ADI25 designated-verifier, BIOW20 interactive) each move a different restriction rather than attacking this cell, which is the pattern the rubric reads as an absent technique. The live source is recent (Nov 2025, revised Feb 2026) and the subarea, pure-GGM SNARG proof-size lower bounds, is narrow.

O2.justification: All load-bearing sources reachable (Gro16 via ePrint 2016/260 and EUROCRYPT proceedings, ADY25 via ePrint 2025/2160), no folklore step, compute bounded to small-field enumeration, and the expected proof shape is a chain of separately statable lemmas: normalise the test matrices, case-split on the bilinear monomial's coefficient, run the sampling attack per case.

reasons: R4: a search over (1,1) NILPs scored by 'completeness minus best affine forgery' is exactly the predicate shape that gets exploited: degenerate sigma, eta = 0 with a vacuously accepting verifier, or a relation whose No-sampler outputs members of the language. Admissibility checks are a precondition, not a nicety.
R1 not applied: the answer exists nowhere, so recall cannot supply it.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $k_1 = k_2 = 1$ with $\eta = 1$: a single pairing-product test, over $\FF_p$ with $m_1, m_2 \le 4$
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Either exhibit a $(1,1)$ split NILP over a small prime field with completeness $\ge 1/2$ and affine-prover soundness error $< 1/p$, or certify by exhaustive enumeration that none exists at $\eta = 1$, $m_1, m_2 \le 4$ and record which structural feature of the test matrix kills every candidate. Provable or refutable in under two pages.
configuration.yield_on_failure: The exhaustive certificate at $\eta = 1$ is itself the first lemma of the impossibility proof, and names the case split the Prover wave would need.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: explicit confirmation that this record is Conjecture 1 (the split-NILP core) and not Conjecture 2 (the compiled purist statement), since the LaTeX is shared with c/0009

title: Groth16 Is Proof-Size Optimal in the Pure Generic Group Model
statement_paraphrase: That every sound purist pairing-based non-interactive argument with completeness error at most 1 - 1/poly for a relation generator with hard decisional problems has proof size at least three group elements.

queries_run: pairing-based SNARG two group elements pure generic group model
Groth16 proof size optimality

evidence.claim: Two group elements are achieved, but only in GGM+ROM: the prover feeds its first proof element through the oracle to derive the verifier's query, which is exactly the channel the purist model lacks. Two elements also suffice in Type I (symmetric) groups. The no-ROM question is ADY25's first open problem.
evidence.citation: Arnon, Dujmovic, Yogev, Pairing-Based SNARGs with Two Group Elements, ePrint 2025/2160

evidence.claim: Implied by c/0008 in the PPE-verifier form: a proof of the split-NILP core plus the compilation gives this statement. The two pages share a byte-identical LaTeX source.
evidence.citation: c/0008 index.qmd relations: implies 0009

evidence.claim: No source found closing the pure-GGM two-element cell.

P1.justification: Same shape as c/0008: an impossibility whose refutation is a construction over finite-dimensional algebra. One notch of the constructive side is lost relative to c/0008, because a purist argument's soundness quantifies over polynomial-query generic provers rather than over sigma-independent affine matrices, so a candidate is harder to score exactly. Still two-sided.
P1.construction_side_dual: A sound, 1/poly-complete purist pairing-based argument of proof size two for a hard relation generator: a CRS of group elements only, a Maurer-generic prover, and proof-independent pairing-product tests derived from phi. Refuting the conjecture means building one.

P2.justification: Identical ladder to c/0008 (one element settled, two elements open, one rung), with the same minus one for the base-case mechanism provably failing at the next rung. The extra compilation step does not add a rung; it is a lemma, not a restriction axis.
P2.restriction_axis: proof size k1 + k2 + kT
P2.settled_base_case: proof size one: impossible, and under OWFs even against arbitrary Maurer-generic verifiers (ADY25 Lemma 6.11)
P2.next_rung: proof size two, one element per source group
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The sampling attack survives, applied to the Mobius curve of accepting pairs; and the compilation from split NILPs to purist arguments is expected to survive unchanged, since the purist prover's matrices depend only on R, phi and the observed equality pattern.

P3.justification: Capped for the same reason as c/0008, with one more source to compose: Gro16, ADY25, and the NILP-to-purist compilation, which the page records in two forms (PPE verifiers and arbitrary generic verifiers). statement_paraphrase: That if the T-fold composition of an ell-local randomized permutation family is negligibly far from floor(log2 n)-wise independent, then it is a pseudorandom permutation.

title: The Censoring Conjecture for AES
statement_paraphrase: That for every t there is a round threshold beyond which approximate t-wise independence of the distinguished censored r-round AES transfers, with the same epsilon, to uncensored r-round AES under independent uniform round keys.

queries_run: t-wise independence SPN AES censored inverse walk Peres Winkler censoring inequality

evidence.claim: Everything the programme proves about the concrete AES S-box is proved about censored AES, with a large fraction of the mixing layers replaced by the identity; the transfer to uncensored AES is the missing step and has not been attempted.
evidence.citation: Jain, Liu, Mizgerd, Pelecanos, Tessaro, Vaikuntanathan, How Fast Does the Inverse Walk Approximate a Random Permutation?; Liu, Pelecanos, Tessaro, Vaikuntanathan, CRYPTO 2023

evidence.claim: The only comparable theorem is Peres and Winkler's censoring inequality for Glauber dynamics on a monotone spin system, and the source paper states its hypotheses do not cover block ciphers.
evidence.citation: Peres and Winkler, Can extra updates delay mixing?

evidence.claim: No source found proving any censoring-to-uncensored transfer for SPNs. The surrounding t-wise independence line (Liu-Tessaro-Vaikuntanathan CRYPTO 2021, Liu-Pelecanos-Tessaro-Vaikuntanathan CRYPTO 2023, Baigneres-Vaudenay SAC 2005) proves bounds for the censored or idealized object rather than transferring them.

P1.justification: An implication between two statistical properties, so the proof side is a comparison inequality with no adversary to construct. The constructive side exists but yields no partial credit toward the statement: the page's Remark on the censoring pattern says the universally-quantified-over-C variant is a strengthening the source does not pose, so a counterexample at an exotic linear layer or censoring set would not refute the conjecture. Scaled-down counterexamples are evidence, not refutations.
P1.construction_side_dual: A scaled-down SPN (a 4-cell state over F_4 or F_16, MDS linear layer, r <= 6) with an exactly computed t-wise transition matrix on which the censored chain is epsilon-close to t-wise independent while the uncensored chain at the same r and epsilon is not. Exactly computable, since AddRoundKey averages over the key and the chain on t-tuples has an exact rational transition matrix.

P2.justification: The productive restriction axis is not t but the censoring set: restore the deleted mixing layers one at a time, from C*(r) down to the empty set. The base case is settled by fiat (it is the hypothesis), the next rung (restore one layer) is nontrivial, well defined and unsettled, and a generalization hypothesis is statable: each restoration should be a data-processing step that cannot increase total variation distance from the uniform t-tuple distribution. No point for a narrow gap: |C*(r)| is a constant fraction of r, so the full ladder is Theta(r) rungs, not three.
P2.restriction_axis: the censoring set: number of mixing layers restored, from C*(r) to the empty set
P2.settled_base_case: C = C*(r), which is the conjecture's hypothesis and is where the published bounds live
P2.next_rung: restore a single mixing layer, |C| = |C*(r)| - 1, at the same r and epsilon
P2.generalization_hypothesis: One-layer restoration is a deterministic post-processing of the state by an invertible linear map applied between two key-addition steps; if the argument is a coupling or a data-processing inequality on the t-tuple chain, it applies unchanged at every subsequent layer.

P3.justification: Capped. The one comparable theorem (Peres-Winkler) provably does not cover block ciphers on the source's own account, so what is needed is a new comparison theorem, not a re-application of an existing one. Composition depth 4 (the inverse-walk paper, LPTV23, LTV21, Peres-Winkler) and a heavy ambient load: the SPN* instantiation the censoring set is defined against, the approximate-t-wise-independence convention, and the treatment of the key schedule all come from the sources' preliminaries.
P3.candidate_technique: comparison of Markov chains: coupling, or a censoring / data-processing inequality on the chain induced on distinct t-tuples

V1.justification: The page is unusually careful and pins almost everything, including two readings explicitly. It loses the single-reading point only because it admits one: 'If the intended reading lets r_th depend on epsilon as well, the conjecture is weaker than the one stated here'. Everything else scores: standard model with independent uniform round keys and the key schedule explicitly out of scope; quantifier order written out in words (epsilon universally quantified, r_th depending on t alone); no adversary to specify since t-wise independence is a statistical property; composition explicitly not applicable; and a vacuous reading easy to state.
V1.idealization: standard model, independent uniform round keys, AES S-box and linear layer concrete
variants_in_play: r_th depending on t alone (the stated reading)
r_th depending on t and epsilon (the weaker reading the page flags)
the distinguished censoring set C*(r) versus universally quantified C
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove it only for epsilon close to 1, or only for r so large that both sides are trivially epsilon-close, so the implication holds with no content about censoring at all.

V2.justification: Maximal, and it is the main reason to spend anything here. The chain induced on distinct t-tuples has an exact rational transition matrix once AddRoundKey is averaged over the uniform key, so for a scaled-down state (4 cells over F_4, t = 2, r <= 6) both sides of the implication are decidable by exact linear algebra: 256 to 65536 states. The predicate hardens with exact rationals plus admissibility checks (S a permutation, L invertible, C actually a subset of the rounds), and there is a scalar to maximise.
V2.finite_instantiation: 4-cell state over F_4 or F_2^4, t = 2, r <= 6, exact rational transition matrix on ordered distinct t-tuples

V3.justification: Lean plus Mathlib is a plausible match: finite Markov chains and total variation distance over a finite state space, with no oracle measure theory and no asymptotics inside the small-case object. The decomposition is not cheap, because the one-layer comparison lemma is precisely what does not exist. An exact small-case computation is a real witness.

O1.justification: Not an aside, and the surrounding subarea (t-wise independence of SPNs) is hot rather than obscure: Tessaro, Vaikuntanathan, Liu, Pelecanos and co-authors have several recent papers on it. The single point is for attempt volume on THIS statement, which is zero: everyone proves censored bounds and nobody has attempted the transfer.

O2.justification: Sources reachable (ePrint plus CRYPTO proceedings) and compute bounded, but a comparison theorem for SPNs is a paper-length development rather than a few pages of separately statable lemmas. There is also a definitional dependency: the censoring set C*(r) is defined by reference to a specific instantiation inside LPTV23, so that paper's construction is load-bearing.

reasons: R1: the censored bounds are published and pre-cutoff, so a produced argument can recall them and present them as the transfer, which is exactly the drift this deduction exists for.
R3: four rungs on the layer-restoration axis, one over the threshold.
R4: the scalar 'TV(uncensored) minus TV(censored)' is exploitable through degenerate linear layers, tiny fields where both sides are zero, and censoring sets that are not the distinguished one.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: One-layer restoration at $t = 2$: if $\mathcal{D}^{(r)}_{C}$ is $\varepsilon$-approximately pairwise independent then so is $\mathcal{D}^{(r)}_{C \setminus \{i\}}$, for a single $i \in C^{*}(r)$
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: On a scaled-down SPN (4 cells over $\FF_4$, $t = 2$, $r \le 6$), compute the exact pairwise transition matrices for $C^{*}(r)$ and for $C^{*}(r) \setminus \{i\}$ and decide whether restoring one layer can ever increase the total variation distance. Either a counterexample at small scale, or a certificate that it never does, in under two pages.
configuration.yield_on_failure: If restoration can increase the distance even at small scale, the pattern-agnostic intuition the whole conjecture rests on is wrong, and that is the finding: it would tell the Case Planner the conjecture is about the specific AES layer and not about censoring in general.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: whether $r_{th}$ may depend on $\varepsilon$
the exact definition of $C^{*}(r)$, which is defined by reference to an instantiation inside LPTV23 rather than self-contained

source_requests.citation: Liu, Pelecanos, Tessaro, Vaikuntanathan, Layout Graphs, Random Walks and the t-wise Independence of SPN Block Ciphers, CRYPTO 2023
source_requests.what_is_needed: The exact SPN* instantiation in which each S-box layer is a run of consecutive (ARK, INV) operations, since C*(r) is defined off it.
source_requests.step_that_collapses_without_it: The hypothesis of the conjecture is not determined, so neither side of the implication can be stated.

title: No Round-Optimal Pairing-Free Blind Signature in the GGM+ROM
statement_paraphrase: That the Dietz-Kastner-Tessaro impossibility for round-optimal blind signatures with group-generic user and verifier algorithms holds for any polynomial bound on the random-oracle queries of User_2 and Verify, not just a logarithmic one.

queries_run: three-move pairing-free blind signature discrete logarithm random oracle model 2026
impossibility round-optimal pairing-free blind signatures ROM

evidence.claim: The source proves the impossibility for at most a logarithmic number of random-oracle queries: 'proving that in a model combining the Random Oracle Model with Maurer's Generic Group Model, no blind signature scheme can be secure if it signs sufficiently long messages while making at most a logarithmic number of random oracle queries'. The polynomial-query case is the remaining gap.
evidence.citation: Dietz, Kastner, Tessaro, On the Impossibility of Round-Optimal Pairing-Free Blind Signatures in the ROM, ePrint 2026/090, CRYPTO 2026

evidence.claim: Round-optimal pairing-free blind signatures DO exist (Kastner, Tessaro, Zaverucha, ePrint 2026/091), but via Fischlin's paradigm with generic NIZKs, which makes non-black-box use of the group and therefore falls outside the group-generic model this conjecture quantifies over. The two results are consistent.
evidence.citation: Kastner, Tessaro, Zaverucha, Round-Optimal Pairing-Free Blind Signatures, ePrint 2026/091

evidence.claim: No source found removing the logarithmic query restriction. The area is moving fast: three-move constructions from DDH appeared in 2026 (ePrint 2026/571 and 2026/593), all on the construction side.

P1.justification: An impossibility against a computationally unbounded but query-bounded adversary class, universally quantified over all schemes. The attack the proof must produce is a construction, which is the machine-friendly part, but the quantification over every candidate scheme is not, and there is no preprocessing or non-uniform advice to push it to zero.
P1.construction_side_dual: A round-optimal (two-message) blind signature scheme with superpolynomial message space whose User_1, User_2 and Verify are transformations of Maurer-generic algorithms with a random oracle for groups, correct, blind against ppt adversaries and one-more unforgeable against unbounded polynomial-query adversaries. Building one refutes the conjecture, and would show the three-move barrier is an artefact of the log-query restriction.

P2.justification: The cleanest ladder in this batch. One explicit restriction axis (q, the total random-oracle queries of User_2 and Verify), a fully settled base case at q = O(log lambda), a next rung that is nontrivial and precisely stated (q = polylog, then q = poly), a statable generalization hypothesis, and a gap of about two rungs. The page's own remark fixes the ladder: 'the conjecture is that the restriction q <= O(log lambda) may be dropped, no other hypothesis being changed'. Monotone: larger q is strictly harder. No deduction for accident: the restriction has one identified cause rather than being a convenient choice.
P2.restriction_axis: q := q_{User_2} + q_{Ver}, the total number of random-oracle queries made by User_2 and Verify
P2.settled_base_case: q(lambda) <= O(log lambda), a theorem of the source
P2.next_rung: q(lambda) = polylog(lambda), then arbitrary polynomial q
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The attacker's structure survives: it still guesses, per hash query, whether key generation or the signer already made that query in this session. What must be replaced is the per-guess accounting, since the source's own lemma bounding failure amplification by 2^q * p is exactly where the 2^{-q} loss enters. A hybrid over queries, or a compression argument on the guess string, replaces the union bound without changing the attack.

P3.justification: One source result, not a cross-paper synthesis: the whole route is inside the source's own proof, replacing its guessing step. That gives a base of 4, minus one for a high ambient convention load: the GGM+ROM formalism (a random oracle for groups, and the notion of a 'transformation of a GGM algorithm'), blind signature syntax, and the one-more-unforgeability conventions all come from the source's preliminaries. No new framework is required, which matches the repo's own reach grade of adaptation.
P3.candidate_technique: hybrid argument / game hopping to replace exhaustive guessing; explicit adversary construction in Maurer's GGM with a group random oracle

V1.justification: Maximal, and earned rather than assumed. The page pins every reading with a dedicated remark: what is already a theorem and exactly which hypothesis is being dropped ('no other hypothesis being changed'); that no query bound is imposed on KeyGen, User_1 or Sign beyond ppt; the idealization named as Maurer's GGM plus a random oracle for groups, with the model defined in the page rather than cited; the superpolynomial message space quantified as lambda^{omega(1)}; blindness against ppt and one-more unforgeability against computationally unbounded polynomial-query adversaries, each with its own definition restated; the concurrency regime determined by the signing oracle in the restated one-more-unforgeability game; and an equivalent restatement in terms of q that makes the quantifier order explicit ('for every polynomial Q there is no scheme as above with q <= Q').
V1.idealization: Maurer's generic group model plus a random oracle for groups (GGM+ROM)
variants_in_play: Maurer's GGM+ROM (the subject)
AGM+ROM, where three-move DL schemes exist
plain ROM with non-black-box group use, where Fischlin-paradigm round-optimal schemes exist
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove the impossibility only for schemes whose Verify makes no random-oracle queries, or only for polynomial-size message spaces, which the lambda^{omega(1)} clause exists precisely to exclude.

V2.justification: Weak, and this is the axis that keeps this out of GO. 'No scheme exists' quantifies over an infinite class, so there is no finite instantiation of the statement and no scalar to score. The one point is for a genuine partial target: against a NAMED candidate scheme (a Schnorr- or Okamoto-Schnorr-shaped two-message template) the attack can be instantiated and checked exactly at small prime order with exact arithmetic. That scores candidates, not the conjecture.
V2.finite_instantiation: a named two-message candidate template at prime order p <= 101, exact arithmetic, attack success measured exactly over all randomness

V3.justification: The games are pseudocodable and EasyCrypt has generic-group and ROM developments, so a tool match exists. But the lemma decomposition is the research content: replacing the 2^{-q} guessing step IS the problem, and no witness short of a full proof is available.

O1.justification: Not an aside, so no provenance bonus: the source names it as the gap its own theorem leaves. But attempt volume is zero, the source is from 2026, and the subarea (GGM+ROM impossibility for round-optimal blind signatures) is narrow even though the neighbouring construction side is crowded.

O2.justification: Every load-bearing source is reachable on ePrint (2026/090, 2026/091, plus Maurer 2005 and Fischlin CRYPTO 2006), no folklore step, no unbounded solver, and the expected development is short and separable: the target is one lemma inside an existing proof, replacing a union bound over 2^q guesses.

reasons: R1 not applied: the source is 2026 and the answer exists nowhere, so recall cannot supply it.
R5 not applied: the pool able to adjudicate a GGM+ROM blind signature impossibility (Kastner, Tessaro, Dietz, Fuchsbauer, Baldimtsi, Loss, Chairattana-Apirom and others) is comfortably above five.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $q(\lambda) = O(\log^2 \lambda)$, every other hypothesis of the source's theorem unchanged
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Replace the source's failure-amplification lemma (the one bounding the loss by $2^{q} p$) with a hybrid over the $q$ hash queries that loses a factor polynomial in $q$ rather than exponential, and check whether the rest of the proof survives the substitution. Two pages, and refutable by exhibiting a scheme on which the hybrid's per-query invariant fails.
configuration.yield_on_failure: If the hybrid cannot be made to work, the reason will identify whether the $2^{-q}$ loss is essential or removable, which is exactly the Lifter's question and is worth writing up either way.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: confirmation that the source's theorem is stated for expected or worst-case query counts
whether the superpolynomial message space hypothesis is retained at the entry rung

title: Three-Move Pairing-Free Blind Signatures from Discrete Log
statement_paraphrase: That there is a three-move blind signature scheme making only black-box use of a pairing-free group, with correctness, blindness and concurrent one-more unforgeability all proved from plain discrete log in the random oracle model alone.

queries_run: three-move pairing-free blind signature discrete logarithm random oracle model 2026

evidence.claim: Three moves in a pairing-free group with one-more unforgeability from DDH in the ROM is achieved, twice and independently, in 2026; both stop at DDH. The DL case remains open.
evidence.citation: Chairattana-Apirom, Reichle, Tessaro, Playing Tag with Okamoto-Schnorr, ePrint 2026/571; Chen, Three-Move Blind Signatures in Pairing-Free Groups, ePrint 2026/593
evidence.eprint_version_date: 2026-03-25 per the paper's own dateline, searched 2026-08-23

evidence.claim: Prior to 2026 every pairing-free three-move scheme needed the algebraic group model on top of the ROM, or at least four moves. Three moves from DL in AGM+ROM and four moves from DL in ROM are the two neighbouring achieved cells.
evidence.citation: Tessaro and Zhu, EUROCRYPT 2022; Abe, EUROCRYPT 2001

evidence.claim: No three-move DL construction found. The page's own caveat anticipated this check and it comes back negative as of the search date.

P1.justification: Maximal. The target IS the construction: explicit algorithms Setup, KeyGen, Sign_1, U_1, Sign_2, U_2, Ver. This is the direction the harness is best at, and the page's own remark on direction confirms the source points this way, noting that refutation would need an impossibility result, 'a different kind of object from a construction'.
P1.construction_side_dual: The statement is itself the construction. The dual on the other side is an impossibility: no three-move group-black-box scheme has concurrent one-more unforgeability from DL, which would be the c/0013-shaped counterpart of this page.

P2.justification: One rung, with three settled neighbouring cells: three moves from DDH in the ROM, three moves from DL in AGM+ROM, four moves from DL in the ROM. The next rung is exactly the target and a generalization hypothesis is statable (keep the tag / Okamoto-Schnorr structure, instantiate the algebraic MAC from DL). Minus one because the base case looks like a special-case accident in the rubric's sense: the source names two obstructions rather than one gap, and DDH is precisely what supplies the linearly-homomorphic extractable commitment that DL does not, so the DDH cell is settled by the very ingredient the DL cell lacks.
P2.restriction_axis: the assumption (DDH -> DL) at fixed round count, or the idealization (AGM+ROM -> ROM) at fixed assumption
P2.settled_base_case: three moves from DDH in the ROM (2026/571, 2026/593); three moves from DL in AGM+ROM; four moves from DL in the ROM
P2.next_rung: three moves from DL in the ROM, black-box in the group
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The tag-based Okamoto-Schnorr structure and the two-move message flow survive; what must be replaced is the algebraic MAC and the linearly-homomorphic extractable commitment, both known from DDH but not black-box from DL.

P3.justification: Capped, on the source's own account: the page records that gluing the known techniques together is explicitly said not to reach it. Two named obstructions have to be overcome at once (the DL-based algebraic MAC, and the message-dependent punctured statement that forces the message into the first move and costs the extra round). Composition depth 3 or more and a high ambient load, including a load-bearing definition that is a reconstruction.
P3.candidate_technique: explicit construction plus game hopping; algebraic MAC and linearly-homomorphic extractable commitment from DL; punctured-statement techniques

V1.justification: Loses the single-reading point, and for the reason that matters most here: the black-box clause, Definition of 'black-box use of the group', is read off the source's framing rather than copied from a definition it states, and the page says outright that this clause 'is what makes Conjecture 1 open' since without it the statement is already settled by Fischlin's paradigm with generic NIZKs. The exact boundary of that clause is therefore the whole content and it is a reconstruction. Everything else is pinned by a dedicated remark: ROM only versus AGM+ROM versus GGM; blindness conditioned on DL rather than unconditional, with the reason; asymptotic rather than concrete reduction, with the reason; concurrent one-more unforgeability; and a nameable vacuous reading.
V1.idealization: random oracle model only, pairing-free group used black-box
variants_in_play: ROM only, group black-box (the subject)
AGM+ROM, where three moves from DL is achieved
ROM with non-black-box group use via generic NIZKs, where the statement is already settled
statistical versus computational blindness
V1.vacuous_reading: Exhibit a scheme whose one-more unforgeability proof handles only sequential signing sessions, or which reaches three moves by wrapping a generic NIZK over the group operations, which is non-black-box use and is what the black-box clause exists to exclude.

V2.justification: Weak. A construction target has no decidable finite instantiation of its security claim, and 'a proof from DL exists' is not a computable score. The one point is for a real Refuter task on candidates: run the known concurrent attacks (ROS / Wagner-style, and the Benhamouda et al. attack shape) against any candidate scheme at small prime order with exact arithmetic, which kills bad candidates cheaply.
V2.finite_instantiation: candidate scheme at prime order p <= 1021, exact arithmetic, known concurrent attacks run to completion

V3.justification: A tool match exists (EasyCrypt or CryptoVerif for blind signature one-more-unforgeability game hopping), but for a NEW construction the lemma-level decomposition is the research content, and there is no witness short of a full proof.

O1.justification: The worst case for the obscurity dividend, despite the source being brand new. The page's own remark says so: the source's reference list contains five works dated 2025 or 2026, two of them to appear at CRYPTO 2026, and this is 'the last remaining cell of a table whose other cells have all been filled over the last two years'. title: Best-First Search Trees Are a Constant-Factor Approximation
statement_paraphrase: That the Huffman-style greedy that repeatedly merges the pair of nodes whose merged keyword tag has the smallest query probability builds a search tree within an absolute constant factor of the optimal tree, for every leaf set and every query distribution.

queries_run: Etemad Mahmoody Evans Optimizing Trees for Static Searchable Encryption approximation ratio greedy best-first
hierarchical clustering minimize sum of union sizes internal nodes greedy approximation ratio binary tree set union

evidence.claim: The only source is a 2018 searchable-encryption systems paper. It leaves open 'a theoretical analysis of the optimality' of best-first without stating a target bound; the constant factor is read off a neighbouring, hedged sentence saying all its algorithms are 'probably within a constant factor of optimal ... when it comes to real data'. No follow-up on the approximation ratio was found.
evidence.citation: Etemad, Mahmoody, Evans, Optimizing Trees for Static Searchable Encryption, ePrint 2018/052

evidence.claim: Exact optimality of best-first is already refuted by the paper's own exhaustive search on eight files, so only the approximation ratio is at stake and the conjecture is not accidentally false at the trivial end.
evidence.citation: same source

evidence.claim: Oblique reformulation searched and came back empty: the objective is a hierarchical-clustering cost (sum over internal nodes of the probability that a random query is consistent with the union of the tags below it), but the hierarchical-clustering literature found is Dasgupta's cost function and metric-space variants, none of which is this objective. The possibility that this is a known problem under another name is the single largest Scout risk here and was not exhausted.
rungs_tried: approximation-algorithms reformulation via hierarchical clustering and sum-of-union-sizes

P1.justification: Two-sided, with a constructive side that does more than yield partial credit: a workload family on which greedy is off by an unbounded factor settles the question outright, and the page says so. The side actually being asked for is the upper bound, which is why this is not a 4.
P1.construction_side_dual: A family of leaf sets and query distributions on which SLC(T)/Opt(L) grows without bound for every T in BF(L,Q). Small members are exactly computable: Opt by exhaustive enumeration over the (2n-3)!! binary trees on n labelled leaves (135135 at n=8, 34.5 million at n=10), greedy by direct simulation over all tie-breakings, the ratio as an exact rational.

P2.justification: The weakest axis, and the honest reason this is not a 26. There is NO settled base case: no bound of any kind is proved for best-first on any class of query distributions, so there is no base-case proof whose surviving feature could be named, and the generalization-hypothesis point cannot be earned. What is earned: the next rung is well defined and singled out by the page itself (Q uniform over single keywords, where the objective collapses to the total Hamming weight of the internal labels), and the gap is narrow, three rungs at most.
P2.restriction_axis: the class of query distributions: single keywords, then disjunctions, then arbitrary monomials
P2.settled_base_case: none for best-first; the page is explicit that no bound of any kind is proved for it
P2.next_rung: Q uniform over single keywords, objective = (1/m) sum over internal nodes of the Hamming weight of the label
P2.generalization_hypothesis: Not available: there is no base-case proof to generalize from. The paper's own proof for the level-optimal algorithm is a shape-only argument that never inspects the algorithm, and best-first is not layered, so nothing in it transfers.

P3.justification: Maximal, and this is the strongest single reason to buy this one. Composition depth 1: there is exactly one source and it supplies no theorem, so nothing has to be composed. The ambient convention load is LOW: the objective, the algorithm and the optimum are all defined self-containedly on the page, with no idealized model and no unstated preliminaries. And the technique class is textbook: greedy approximation ratios are proved by exchange or charging arguments against a fractional or structural lower bound on the optimum, which is Huffman's own proof shape. No new framework is required.
P3.candidate_technique: greedy approximation analysis: exchange / charging arguments against a structural or LP-relaxation lower bound on Opt, in the style of Huffman optimality

V1.justification: Maximal, and it is the cleanest statement in the corpus. One reading, with the tie-breaking ambiguity resolved explicitly in the strong direction (the conjecture quantifies over every T in BF(L,Q), not over one canonical tie-break). No idealization at all, so the model-variant hazard that dominates the rest of this corpus is simply absent. The quantifier order is written out and the constant is existentially quantified first, before m, n, L and Q. No adversary to specify. Composition not applicable. And a vacuous reading is easy to name.
V1.idealization: none: finite combinatorics over binary trees and rational probabilities
variants_in_play: every tree in BF(L,Q) (the stated, strong reading)
one canonical tie-breaking rule (a partial answer the page says is worth reporting as such)
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove the bound only for leaf sets whose tags all have Hamming weight one and Q uniform over single keywords, where every binary tree has the same cost and the ratio is 1 for trivial reasons; or restrict to n <= 8, where the paper's own exhaustive search already reports greedy essentially matching brute force.

V2.justification: Maximal. The statement is decidable at named finite parameters by exact rational arithmetic: for n <= 10 and m <= 6, Opt is an exhaustive minimum over binary trees and greedy is deterministic once tie-breakings are enumerated, so the ratio is an exact rational. The predicate hardens with rationals only plus admissibility checks (Q sums to one and is supported on monomials, tags lie in {0,1}^m, Opt > 0, all tie-breakings enumerated rather than sampled). And the search object is small with a scalar to maximise, which is exactly the shape that construction search is good at.
V2.finite_instantiation: n <= 10 leaves, m <= 6 keywords, Q of support <= 8; Opt by exhaustive tree enumeration, ratio as an exact rational

V3.justification: Lean plus Mathlib is a real match, not a nominal one: finite binary trees, rationals, and a sum over internal nodes, with no measure theory over oracle spaces and no asymptotics inside the object. A machine-checkable witness short of a proof exists in two forms, an exact counterexample instance and an exhaustive small-n certificate. The decomposition point is withheld: finding the right lower bound on Opt to charge the greedy merges against is the research content, and nobody has attempted it, so it cannot be called cheap to write.

O1.justification: A strong obscurity dividend. The provenance is an aside in the rubric's exact sense: a hedged sentence adjacent to the paper's open-questions remark, in a systems paper about encrypted search indices, never returned to. Attention volume is zero, not low: the citing literature is about searchable encryption, and no paper attempts the ratio. The recency point is withheld because the source is 2018, not recent, even though the subarea is narrow. Separately worth recording: this may already be a corollary of something in the approximation-algorithms literature under a different name, which raises Scout priority without changing attackability.

O2.justification: The single source is open access and is the only load-bearing one, there is no folklore step, the compute profile is bounded by explicit parameter caps rather than by an open-ended solver call, and the expected proof is a few pages as a chain of separately statable lemmas: a lower bound on Opt, a per-merge charging lemma, and a merge-order exchange lemma.

reasons: R4: the scalar SLC(T)/Opt(L) is exactly the predicate shape that gets exploited. Division by zero when every internal label has zero query mass, Q not normalised, Q supported outside the monomial family, duplicate leaf tags, and sampling rather than enumerating tie-breakings are all wins that are not counterexamples. Exact rationals plus admissibility checks that raise are a precondition here, not a nicety.
R1 not applied: the area is not well studied and the answer exists nowhere. The adjacent risk that this is a renamed known problem is recorded under O1 as a Scout priority instead.
R5 not applied: greedy approximation ratios on trees can be adjudicated by a large community.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $\Qd$ uniform over single keywords, where $\SLC_{\Qd}(T) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{u \in I(T)} \HW(\bar u)$: is best-first within an absolute constant of the minimum total Hamming weight of internal labels?
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Exhaustive search at $n \le 10$, $m \le 6$ over the single-keyword case: either an instance with $\SLC/\Opt \ge 3$, which already rules out the small constants and tells the Prover what shape to expect, or an exact certificate that the ratio never exceeds a specific rational at those parameters, which is the base case a charging argument would be built on. Provable or refutable in under two pages.
configuration.yield_on_failure: Either outcome is a result. A growing ratio in $n$ refutes the conjecture and settles the paper's question; a flat ratio pins the constant to aim at and identifies the worst-case instance family the charging argument has to be tight on.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: whether a bound for one canonical tie-breaking rule counts as an answer or only as a partial one
whether the single-keyword case alone is an acceptable freeze, which the page's own remark says the drafter would regard as the real content

title: Level-Optimal Search Trees Beyond Disjunctive Queries
statement_paraphrase: That the level-by-level minimum-weight-matching tree construction is within a log n factor of optimal for some class of query distributions strictly larger than the disjunctive ones.

queries_run: Etemad Mahmoody Evans Optimizing Trees for Static Searchable Encryption approximation ratio
level-optimal search tree conjunctive queries encrypted search

evidence.claim: Proved for every distribution supported on disjunctive queries, where the log n factor is also shown necessary. Wide open for conjunctive queries, where the paper's own proof technique demonstrably fails: for a disjunctive query a node is consistent only if a matching file lies beneath it, so every balanced tree is within a log factor, and the paper exhibits an AND query consistent with a node under which no file satisfies it.
evidence.citation: Etemad, Mahmoody, Evans, Optimizing Trees for Static Searchable Encryption, ePrint 2018/052

evidence.claim: No follow-up found on either the class or the bound; the citing literature is about searchable encryption rather than about the combinatorial question.

definitions_needing_repair: The class C itself. The conjecture asserts 'there are a class C of query distributions, strictly containing every distribution supported on disjunctive queries, and an absolute constant c' such that the bound holds. Identifying C is part of the problem, not a hypothesis of it, and the page says so: the authors state it as a conjecture without naming the broader class. As written, C = disjunctions plus one arbitrary extra distribution satisfies the letter of the statement, so it is trivially true and the campaign would freeze a vacuity.

Which of the three readings on the page is the target: Conjecture 1 with C unnamed (as written), Conjecture 2 with C the class of ALL distributions over monomials (the maximal formalization, also on the page), or the intermediate reading the page's own remark names as the one that discharges the paper's intent, C the distributions supported on conjunctive queries. These are three different problems with three different difficulties.

Tie-breaking. The minimum-weight perfect matching need not be unique, so the algorithm's output is a set of trees; the page quantifies over every tree in LO(L,Q), which it flags as a deliberate strengthening of the paper's own single-tree formulation.

The page already supplies the seed: half the files carrying {Female, Dept1} and half {Male, Dept2} at alternate leaves of a balanced tree, against the query Female AND Dept2.

title: No Key Agreement from Garbling One-Way-Function Circuits
statement_paraphrase: That there is no fully black-box construction of key agreement, at any polynomial round complexity, from an oracle providing a random function together with garbling of circuits with gates for that function.

queries_run: Garg Hajiabadi Mahmoody Mohammed limits on the power of garbling techniques for public-key encryption rounds

evidence.claim: Proved in full for two messages, which is public-key encryption (the source's Theorem 4.1). The constant-round extension is sketched in the paper's Appendix A without a theorem, its security half deferred to the PKE proof. Round complexity growing with the security parameter is untouched.
evidence.citation: Garg, Hajiabadi, Mahmoody, Mohammed, Limits on the Power of Garbling Techniques for Public-Key Encryption, ePrint 2018/555

evidence.claim: The obstruction is named and quantitative: the compilation removes garbling-evaluation queries one round at a time and inflates communication by a polynomial factor per round, so super-constant rounds compound into a tower of polynomials. The plain-random-oracle analogue has been round-free since Impagliazzo-Rudich, which is the reason to expect a round-free argument exists here too.
evidence.citation: Impagliazzo and Rudich, STOC 1989

evidence.claim: No source found extending the separation to super-constant rounds.

P1.justification: An impossibility universally quantified over every pair of oracle interactive algorithms and every oracle security reduction, delivered as an oracle separation. The machine-friendly part, constructing the attacker, sits inside a quantifier the harness cannot search over. No preprocessing or non-uniform advice, so not a zero.
P1.construction_side_dual: A key-agreement protocol relative to the GCOWF oracle, with round complexity growing in the security parameter, together with a reduction showing that breaking it breaks either the one-wayness of f or the garbling security. Since the two-message case is ruled out, any such protocol must use its extra rounds to do something no two-message protocol can, which is a searchable structural question at small oracle domains.

P2.justification: A clean single-axis ladder with a fully settled base case and a quantitative, named obstruction rather than a conceptual one. Base case: two messages, a theorem. Next rung: super-constant rounds, since constant rounds is sketched. The generalization hypothesis is statable and the page states it: the per-round compilation survives, and what has to change is the accounting, from a polynomial factor per round to an accounting that does not pay per round. Gap of about two rungs. Monotone in rounds, and the base case is not an accident: two messages is public-key encryption, a natural anchor, and the plain-ROM analogue is round-free.
P2.restriction_axis: round complexity of the key-agreement protocol
P2.settled_base_case: two messages, equivalently public-key encryption (source Theorem 4.1); 2m rounds for constant m sketched in Appendix A without a theorem
P2.next_rung: round complexity growing with the security parameter, e.g. O(log lambda) rounds
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The round-by-round compilation that removes garbling-evaluation queries survives unchanged. What must be replaced is its cost accounting: the polynomial communication inflation per round has to become an amortised bound, since Impagliazzo-Rudich shows the analogous plain-oracle argument needs no per-round payment at all.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2, the source plus Impagliazzo-Rudich, giving a base of 3, minus one for a high ambient convention load: the fully-black-box definitional framework, the GCOWF oracle, correctness and security of a garbling scheme for oracle-aided circuits relative to f, and the compilation itself are all carried from the source's preliminaries. No new framework: the repo's own reach grade is adaptation, and the page says a proof needs an accounting that does not pay per round, not a new separation technique.
P3.candidate_technique: black-box separation by oracle construction, with an amortised (rather than per-round) accounting of the query-removal compilation

V1.justification: Loses the single-reading point, and for a reason specific to this literature: the black-box flavour is load-bearing and this page's Definition is, on its own account, a transposition mirroring the source's definition rather than a copy of it. The sibling record c/0020 shows how much turns on flavour (fully versus semi versus for-all-exists-semi, plain versus infinitely-often primitives). Everything else scores: the GCOWF oracle named and defined; the quantifier structure written out in full as 'for every (A,B) and every S there exist f and L such that at least one of the following fails'; the adversary and reduction classes specified as oracle PPT with no round bound beyond that; composition not applicable; and a vacuous reading easy to name.
V1.idealization: an idealized oracle providing a random function f together with garbling of oracle-aided circuits with f-gates (GCOWF)
variants_in_play: fully black-box (as stated)
semi-black-box and for-all-exists-semi-black-box, the flavours that matter in the sibling c/0020
two-message (settled) versus constant-round (sketched) versus super-constant (the target)
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove it only for two-message protocols, which is the source's Theorem 4.1, or only for constant round complexity, which its Appendix A already sketches: both are inside the quantifier the conjecture exists to remove.

V2.justification: Weak, and it is what keeps this off the GO list. An oracle separation quantified over all protocols and all reductions has no finite instantiation in which the statement is decidable, so the first point is not available and the hardening point is moot. The one point is for a genuine search object: a candidate multi-round key-agreement protocol relative to a small-domain GCOWF oracle, scored by the eavesdropper's exact success, which at least kills bad candidates cheaply.
V2.finite_instantiation: none for the statement; a candidate protocol at a small oracle domain can be scored exactly

V3.justification: Nothing here. No assistant covers black-box separations built from oracle constructions with measure-one arguments: EasyCrypt and SSProve do game hopping between fixed games, not quantification over all reductions. The amortised accounting is itself the research content, so the decomposition point is unavailable. No witness short of a full proof.

The provenance is an aside in the rubric's exact sense: the source poses it as a future direction rather than as a numbered conjecture, and the page records that the direction of the answer is the paper's evident expectation but is never asserted by it. But an oracle separation for super-constant rounds is a paper-length development, not a short chain of separately statable lemmas: the compilation and its accounting are entangled across the whole argument.

title: One-Way Functions Are Black-Box Useless for Key Agreement
statement_paraphrase: That for every auxiliary primitive Z, any semi-black-box reduction of key agreement to the pair (one-way functions, Z) can be replaced by one to Z alone, with no restriction on rounds, correctness or query counts.

queries_run: Couteau Farshim Mahmoody black-box uselessness key agreement central open problem sampler adaptivity

evidence.claim: The source calls this its central open problem: 'the central open problem left by our work is that of black-box uselessness of OWFs for arbitrary key agreement protocols', adding that 'given our BBU results for special classes of KA protocols, this conjecture may well be within reach', while 'a straightforward generalization seems to require a refined sampler technique with low adaptivity'.
evidence.citation: Couteau, Farshim, Mahmoody, Black-Box Uselessness: Composing Separations in Cryptography, ePrint 2021/016

evidence.claim: Settled for three restricted protocol classes: constant-query with perfect correctness, constant-round constant-query with imperfect correctness, and Merkle-type (the source's Theorems 4.1, 4.9, 4.12). The recorded reason the general case stalls is that the recursive use of inverters inside the sampler blows up query complexity to the auxiliary oracle, limiting the argument to a constant number of sampling steps.
evidence.citation: same source

evidence.claim: No source found settling the general case.

P1.justification: Sits between the rubric's 1 and 3 and is scored at 2 deliberately. The object to be produced is a construction, a low-adaptivity sampler that converts one reduction into another, which is the machine-friendly direction. What kills it is the quantifier: the construction has to work for EVERY auxiliary primitive Z, with arbitrary rounds, arbitrary correctness and arbitrary query counts, and that universal quantification is not something construction search can enter.
