title: Simon-Oracle Product Hardness (the amplification conjecture, strong version)
statement_paraphrase: That the hardness of inverting an arbitrary epsilon-secure one-way function and the hardness of inverting a random permutation multiply, even for an adversary given Simon's recursive collision-finder oracle for the permutation.

queries_run: Couteau Farshim Mahmoody Simon oracle amplification conjecture product hardness collision finder

evidence.claim: Open. The version without the collision finder is known only when the one-way function is itself a random oracle; with an arbitrary one-way function, with or without the collision finder, nothing is established.
evidence.citation: Couteau, Farshim, Mahmoody, Black-Box Uselessness: Composing Separations in Cryptography, ePrint 2021/016

evidence.claim: This is the load-bearing lemma for the sibling record c/0019: the two relaxations of 'OWFs are black-box helpful for CRHFs', distributional and class-reduction helpfulness, are proved conditional on exactly this conjecture. Resolving it therefore delivers partial progress on another page in this corpus.
evidence.citation: same source, Theorem 6.8

evidence.claim: The source's displayed inequality contains a typo, writing P(x_1) where F(x_1) is meant, and leaves two quantifier readings implicit; the page repairs the typo and fixes both readings in the standard way (the polynomial existentially quantified after the adversary; epsilon-security required only against machines with access to F, not to the random permutation).
evidence.citation: c/0021 latex/main.tex, Remarks on the typo and on readings

P1.justification: A hardness lower bound against an oracle-aided PPT adversary, holding for a measure one of random permutations and collision finders. The proof direction is an inequality; the machine-friendly side is the refutation.
P1.construction_side_dual: An oracle-aided adversary A that, given F(x_1) and RP(x_2) and access to F, RP and Simon's collision finder, outputs both preimages with probability substantially exceeding epsilon(lambda) * poly(lambda) / 2^lambda, presumably by using the collision finder to correlate the two inversions. At lambda = 2 or 3 the whole space of permutations of a 4- or 8-element domain (24 or 40320 permutations) and of functions F on that domain is enumerable, so a candidate adversary's success is an exact rational.

P2.justification: Two entangled restriction axes with a settled corner: whether F is a random oracle or arbitrary, and whether the collision finder is present. The corner that is known is 'no collision finder, F a random oracle'; the next rung (no collision finder, arbitrary F) is well defined and unsettled, and a generalization hypothesis is statable. Minus one because the base case is a special-case accident in the rubric's sense: the random-oracle case is proved using the structure of the oracle's table, and an arbitrary epsilon-secure F offers no table to count over, so the base-case mechanism does not survive the very step being climbed.
P2.restriction_axis: whether F is a random oracle or an arbitrary epsilon-secure function, crossed with presence of the collision finder
P2.settled_base_case: no collision finder, F itself a random oracle
P2.next_rung: no collision finder, F an arbitrary epsilon-secure one-way function
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The surviving feature is that the two inversion tasks are independent given the adversary's transcript. In the random-oracle case that independence is read off the oracle's table by a counting or compression argument; for arbitrary F it has to be derived from epsilon-security alone, which is what a multi-instance or direct-product reduction is for.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2 (the source plus Simon's separation), base 3, minus one for a high ambient convention load: Simon's collision finder with recursive gates, measure-one quantification over permutation families, and the surrounding uselessness framework are all carried context. Not capped: direct-product hardness amplification relative to an oracle is a named, standard technique class (multi-instance reductions, XOR and hardcore lemmas), and what is missing is its instantiation against Simon's oracle rather than a new framework.
P3.candidate_technique: direct-product hardness amplification relative to an oracle; multi-instance and auxiliary-input reductions; compression against the collision finder

V1.justification: Loses the single-reading point, and honestly so: the source's displayed inequality contains a typo that the page repairs, and two further readings (the quantifier on the polynomial, and whether epsilon-security holds against machines that also query the permutation) are supplied by the compositor rather than by the source. The second of those is substantive, not cosmetic. Everything else scores: the idealization named and defined (random permutation plus Simon's recursive collision finder); quantifiers pinned explicitly by the readings remark; the adversary class fully specified as oracle-aided PPT with access to all three oracles; composition not applicable; and a vacuous reading nameable.
V1.idealization: random permutation with Simon's recursive collision-finder oracle
variants_in_play: epsilon-security of F against F-only machines (the fixed reading)
epsilon-security against machines that also query RP and the collision finder
with and without the collision finder
F a random oracle versus arbitrary
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove it only for epsilon(lambda) = 1, where the claimed bound poly(lambda)/2^lambda is just the trivial bound for inverting a random permutation and the product structure carries no content at all.

V2.justification: The first point is withheld: the statement carries a poly(lambda) slack and an asymptotic 'for all sufficiently large lambda', so it is not decided at any finite lambda, only probed. The second and third are earned: at lambda = 2 or 3 the enumeration is exact over rationals, epsilon-security of a candidate F is itself exactly checkable, and admissibility checks can enforce it; and a candidate adversary is a bounded-depth decision tree over the three oracles, which is a search-representable object with the success probability as its scalar score.
V2.finite_instantiation: lambda in {2,3}: all permutations of a 4- or 8-element domain and all F on it, exact rational arithmetic, with the polynomial pinned to a constant

V3.justification: No tool match: measure-one arguments over permutation families with a recursive collision-finder oracle are outside what any listed assistant covers, and the argument for arbitrary F does not exist so its decomposition cannot be called cheap. The one point is for a real witness: an explicit adversary at small lambda with an exactly computed success probability exceeding the bound, with the polynomial pinned, is a counterexample certificate.

O1.justification: The maximum obscurity dividend in this batch, and it is a real one. The provenance is precisely the rubric's aside shape: a technical amplification conjecture stated in Section 6 of a single 2021 ePrint in order to condition two relaxations of a different conjecture, and never returned to. Attempt volume is zero. The source is recent enough and the subarea, hardness amplification relative to Simon's oracle, is as narrow as this corpus gets. Worth recording separately: it is plausibly a corollary of a general direct-product theorem nobody has connected to Simon's oracle, which raises Scout priority without changing attackability.

O2.justification: One reachable source, no folklore step, bounded compute, and the expected shape is short: a product-hardness lemma relative to an oracle plausibly runs a few pages as a chain (a hybrid over the two inversion tasks, a compression or counting step against the collision finder, a union bound).

reasons: R4: the scalar 'probability of outputting both preimages' is exploitable through a degenerate F that is not actually epsilon-secure at the tested lambda, through an adversary that exceeds its query budget, and through tiny lambda where the polynomial slack swallows everything. Admissibility checks that verify epsilon-security exactly are the precondition.
R5: hardness amplification specifically against Simon's recursive collision finder is adjudicable by a very small pool.
R1 not applied: nothing is established for arbitrary F, so recall cannot supply the answer.

title: Classical Attacks on CAQB Key Agreement Without Perfect Completeness
statement_paraphrase: That a purely classical eavesdropper with polynomially many expected queries recovers the key of any classical-Alice quantum-Bob key agreement protocol in the QROM, when completeness is merely negligibly imperfect rather than exact.

queries_run: Austrin Chung Chung Fu Lin Mahmoody impossibility key agreement quantum random oracles perfect completeness

evidence.claim: Settled for perfect completeness by the source's Theorem 3.1. The argument's final step works by showing that some oracle is consistent both with a fake Alice view the eavesdropper samples and with Bob's real state, then invoking that any such oracle forces the two keys to agree; if the honest parties may fail with even negligible probability that last step gives nothing, and the authors say so and leave the question open.
evidence.citation: Austrin, Chung, Chung, Fu, Lin, Mahmoody, On the Impossibility of Key Agreements from Quantum Random Oracles, ePrint 2022/218 (report number as recorded on the page)

evidence.claim: The near-miss barrier does NOT apply to the statement as narrowed. Widening it back to a quantum Alice would, by the source's Theorem 7.6, make it imply the Simulation Conjecture; the page deliberately restricts to the classical-Alice case, which is what the source's own sentence refers to. So G1 does not fire, but it fires one step away.
evidence.citation: c/0022 latex/main.tex, Remark on scope

evidence.claim: No source found removing the perfect-completeness hypothesis.

P1.justification: The object to be produced is an explicit algorithm, a classical eavesdropper, and the source already has one for the perfect case (its Construction 3.7 and Lemma 3.8) that has to be made noise-tolerant. That is the machine-friendly direction. It is a 3 rather than a 4 because the algorithm must work for EVERY protocol family in the class, so the statement as a whole is an impossibility result even though the deliverable is a construction; producing the attack for a restricted protocol class yields real partial credit.
P1.construction_side_dual: A CAQB key agreement protocol with negligible but nonzero completeness error that resists every classical eavesdropper making polynomially many expected queries. Building one refutes the conjecture and would show that imperfect completeness is not a technical convenience but the source of real quantum advantage in this model.

P2.justification: A single clean axis (the completeness error), a fully settled base case (gamma = 0, Theorem 3.1), a well-defined unsettled next rung, and a generalization hypothesis that is statable and stated. Minus one because the base case's mechanism provably fails one rung up: the page records that the final step uses perfect completeness in a way that no known weakening survives, which is exactly the special-case-accident trigger.
P2.restriction_axis: completeness error gamma
P2.settled_base_case: gamma = 0, perfect completeness, the source's Theorem 3.1
P2.next_rung: gamma = 1/poly, then gamma negligible
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The attack's structure survives: sample a fake Alice view consistent with the transcript, then find an oracle consistent both with that fake view and with Bob's real state. What must be replaced is the final inference, which currently reads 'any such oracle forces the keys to agree'; at nonzero gamma that has to become an averaging or robustness statement over the consistent oracles.

P3.justification: Capped. The route needs a genuinely new mechanism for the final step, not a re-run of the old one: the page states that the step uses perfect completeness in a way that no known weakening survives. That is the framework's own warning case, a short proof turning on one new idea rather than a long proof of locally routine steps. Composition depth 1 in its favour, and the ambient load is high (the CAQB model, superposition access for Bob only, expected rather than worst-case query counts, and the Simulation-Conjecture context one step away).

title: The Polynomial Compatibility Conjecture
statement_paraphrase: That for some finite abelian group there is an inverse-polynomial-in-degree influence threshold below which any two distributions over unit-norm degree-d functions with small average influences must contain one function from each whose product is nonzero somewhere.

queries_run: polynomial compatibility conjecture Austrin Chung Chung Fu Lin Mahmoody influence degree abelian group
Chung Lin Mahmoody black-box separations non-interactive commitments quantum world

evidence.claim: Proved at one end and refuted at the other, with the target strictly between: proved for influences below |Y|^{-d}/d by the work that introduced it, refuted for delta >= 1/(2d) in that paper's Appendix B, which also shows the degree and influence hypotheses are needed on both distributions rather than one. Everything between |Y|^{-d}/d and 1/(2d) is open, and any delta that is 1/poly(d, log|Y|) already suffices for the downstream polynomial-query attack.
evidence.citation: Austrin, Chung, Chung, Fu, Lin, Mahmoody, On the Impossibility of Key Agreements from Quantum Random Oracles

evidence.claim: The later paper consumes the conjecture throughout without attempting it: its Theorem 1.1, Section 4, Lemma 4.4 and Construction 4.5 are all conditional on it, used to rule out quantum black-box constructions of non-interactive commitments from post-quantum one-way functions. Report number and year are flagged on the page as not yet checked by a human.
evidence.citation: Chung, Lin, Mahmoody, Black-Box Separations for Non-Interactive Commitments in a Quantum World, ePrint 2023/570

evidence.claim: Kinship with the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture is noted by the source (AA is likewise known only for exponentially small influences), but no implication in either direction is claimed, so the transferred-barrier gate does not fire here as it does for c/0056.
evidence.citation: Aaronson and Ambainis, The Need for Structure in Quantum Speedups, ITCS 2011

evidence.claim: No source found closing the inverse-polynomial regime from either end.
rungs_tried: arXiv and ECCC search on the Fourier formulation

P1.justification: Two-sided, with real structure on both sides. The proof direction is a Fourier inequality, but it carries an unusual constructive element: the group is existentially quantified, so exhibiting a single finite abelian group (Z_2 will do) and proving the statement for it settles the conjecture affirmatively. The refutation direction is an explicit pair of distributions, which is a construction with a scalar score, and partial progress on it, pushing the refuted regime below 1/(2d), narrows the gap and is publishable on its own. Not a 4 because the asymmetry runs the other way for refutation: a counterexample must rule out every finite abelian group.
P1.construction_side_dual: An explicit pair of distributions over unit-norm degree-d functions on Y^N with average influences at most delta and disjointly supported non-vanishing sets, for some delta strictly below 1/(2d). At Y = Z_2, N <= 6 and d <= 3 the search space of support patterns is finite, so a candidate is exactly checkable and the largest refutable delta is a scalar to minimise.

P2.justification: The strongest ladder feature in the corpus after c/0010: both ends of the parameter range are settled, one by proof and one by refutation, so the work is entirely in locating a threshold that is known to exist somewhere in a bracketed interval. Explicit axis, settled base case, well-defined next rung, statable generalization hypothesis. Minus one because the base case looks like a special-case accident: |Y|^{-d}/d is exactly the regime where a naive union bound over the N coordinates survives, and 1/poly(d) is where it stops, which is also where the analogous Aaronson-Ambainis programme has been stuck for twenty years.
P2.restriction_axis: the average-influence threshold delta as a function of d
P2.settled_base_case: delta <= |Y|^{-d}/d, proved by the originating work
P2.next_rung: delta = |Y|^{-d/2}, or delta = 2^{-sqrt d}, i.e. any super-polynomially small but not exponentially small threshold
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The surviving feature is the reduction to a single-coordinate influence bound: the exponentially-small-influence proof controls all N coordinates by a bound that is uniform in N, and the group being existentially quantified means one may fix Y = Z_2 and use hypercontractivity or a level-d inequality in place of the union bound, without changing the shape of the argument.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2 (the originating work's proved regime, plus a hypercontractive or level-k inequality from the analysis-of-functions literature), giving a base of 3, and no ambient-load deduction on a second reading: the page defines degree, influence, the dual group and the unit-l2 normalisation self-containedly, and the quantum-state formulation is flagged as a sibling variant rather than required context. Not capped: the candidate techniques are named and standard, and the object is a Fourier inequality rather than a new framework. [Corrected on re-score: the first pass applied a HIGH-load deduction while labelling the load MEDIUM.]
P3.candidate_technique: hypercontractivity and Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups; level-k inequalities; the polynomial method; sum-of-squares for the small-parameter certificates

V1.justification: Maximal, and the page earns it by anticipating the exact misreadings. One reading, and the page defends the precise form of the bound against a weaker one with a worked counterexample: writing delta(d) >= d^{-c} instead of c_1 d^{-c_2} would force delta(1) = 1, and over Z_2 with N = 1 the degree-one unit-norm functions (1+x)/sqrt 2 and (1-x)/sqrt 2 have influence 1/2 and vanish at opposite points, so point masses on them refute it. No idealized model at all: this is discrete Fourier analysis. The quantifier structure is pinned by its own remark (delta may depend on d but not on N; the group is existentially quantified, so one group suffices for a proof while a refutation must rule out all of them). No adversary and no composition regime. And a very concrete vacuous reading.
V1.idealization: none: discrete Fourier analysis over a finite abelian group
variants_in_play: the combinatorial form over distributions of functions (the subject)
the equivalent (Y, delta, d, N)-quantum-state form used downstream, reached by a conversion lemma
delta(d) >= c_1 d^{-c_2} (correct) versus delta(d) >= d^{-c} (false at d=1)
V1.vacuous_reading: Choose c_1 so small that c_1 d^{-c_2} <= |Y|^{-d}/d over the whole range of d actually treated, so the claimed inverse-polynomial threshold is the already-proved exponentially-small regime wearing a polynomial's clothes.

V2.justification: Maximal. At Y = Z_2 with N <= 6 and d <= 3 the non-vanishing support of a function is a subset of a finite cube, so the existence of a compatible pair reduces to a finite family of feasibility problems over support patterns, decidable by exact rational linear or semidefinite programming; and the refuted end at 1/(2d) is already witnessed by explicit counterexamples, so the boundary is computable rather than hypothetical. The predicate hardens with exact rationals and interval arithmetic plus admissibility checks (unit l2 norm, degree bound, average-influence bound, all verifiable exactly). And the scalar is immediate: the largest delta at which a counterexample exists, at fixed (Y, d, N).
V2.finite_instantiation: Y = Z_2, N <= 6, d <= 3: exact rational LP/SDP feasibility over the finite family of non-vanishing support patterns

title: Four-Party NIKE with Quadratic Security in Maurer's Generic Group Model
statement_paraphrase: That there is a four-party non-interactive key exchange in Maurer's label-free generic group model whose honest parties make about n queries while every eavesdropper making o(n^2) queries has vanishing advantage.

queries_run: fine-grained non-interactive key exchange generic group model Maurer Shoup Afshar Couteau Mahmoody Sadeghi follow-up
fine-grained NIKE revisited quadratic Maurer

evidence.claim: The page's state of the art is stale, and the page anticipated this: its own caveat says the citing papers had not been checked. A CRYPTO 2024 follow-up achieves a four-party NIKE with a hardness gap up to N^{1.6} IN MAURER'S MODEL, assuming the existence of non-uniformly secure injective pseudorandom generators with exponential hardness, and separately achieves the quadratic gap in the standard model. The paper is explicit that the quadratic gap in Maurer's model remains open.
evidence.citation: Bauer, Couteau, Sadeghi, Fine-Grained Non-Interactive Key Exchange, Revisited, ePrint 2024/834, CRYPTO 2024

evidence.claim: The N^{1.6} construction does not settle the statement on this page, because it is CONDITIONAL on an injective-PRG assumption, whereas the conjecture as stated demands vanishing advantage against computationally unbounded query-bounded eavesdroppers, i.e. an information-theoretic guarantee in the generic group model. The two are different objects, and conflating them is the drift trap this record exists to flag.

The source achieves the analogous protocol in Shoup's model (its Construction 9, Theorem 10) and proves that no protocol in Maurer's model can do better than quadratic for any party count at least three, which is where the ceiling comes from. It names building the Maurer-model protocol as one of the two routes to closing its own gap.
evidence.citation: Afshar, Couteau, Mahmoody, Sadeghi, Fine-Grained Non-Interactive Key-Exchange: Constructions and Lower Bounds, ePrint 2023/571, EUROCRYPT 2023

evidence.claim: A further paper pursues fine-grained NIKE without idealized models, which is adjacent rather than on point.

Settled: quadratic in Shoup's model (the source's Construction 9 and Theorem 10), and N^{1.6} in Maurer's model conditionally (CRYPTO 2024). Next rung: N^{1.6} unconditionally, or N^{1.8} conditionally. Generalization hypothesis statable: the Shoup construction's only label-dependent step is recovering a missing half-exponent by a square-root-time generic discrete-log computation on labels, and the follow-up shows that step can be replaced, so the partial-collision structure is what survives. Minus one because the base case is a special-case accident in the sharpest possible sense: the Shoup construction turns on labels, and Maurer's model has no labels by definition.

P2.settled_base_case: e = 2 in Shoup's model, unconditionally; e = 1.6 in Maurer's model, assuming exponentially hard non-uniformly secure injective PRGs
P2.next_rung: e = 1.6 in Maurer's model without the PRG assumption, or e = 1.8 with it

title: Quadratic Attack on Three-Party NIKE in Shoup's Generic Group Model
statement_paraphrase: That every three-party non-interactive key exchange in Shoup's labelled generic group model, with n queries per party, is broken by an eavesdropper making O(n^2) queries.

evidence.claim: Settled by the source in Maurer's model for every party count at least three, including imperfect correctness: a randomness-switching lemma (its Lemma 19) shows the first party's key is recoverable from three keys computed under resampled randomness, giving an O(alpha)-query attack (its Theorem 20), with zero tests handled separately for general protocols. Shoup's model is open, and the source names closing the gap as an interesting question.
evidence.citation: Afshar, Couteau, Mahmoody, Sadeghi, Fine-Grained Non-Interactive Key-Exchange: Constructions and Lower Bounds, ePrint 2023/571, EUROCRYPT 2023

evidence.claim: The CRYPTO 2024 follow-up works the other half of the gap (constructions), reaching N^{1.6} in Maurer's model under an injective-PRG assumption and quadratic in the standard model; on the abstract as fetched it does not address extending the impossibility to Shoup's model, so this cell remains open.
evidence.citation: Bauer, Couteau, Sadeghi, Fine-Grained Non-Interactive Key Exchange, Revisited, ePrint 2024/834, CRYPTO 2024

It is a 3 rather than a 4 because the attack must work against every three-party protocol in Shoup's model, and partial credit is available: the attack for protocols with restricted label operations is a real intermediate result.
P1.construction_side_dual: A three-party NIKE in Shoup's model whose honest parties make n queries and which resists every O(n^2)-query eavesdropper: that is, a protocol that genuinely exploits labels (hashing, sorting, or a square-root-time generic discrete log on them) to beat the quadratic ceiling that Maurer's model imposes. Minus one because the base case's mechanism provably fails at the next rung: randomness switching resamples the parties' randomness, and in Shoup's model that changes labels the parties may already have hashed or committed to, which is exactly the power the source's own positive result uses to beat Maurer's ceiling.
P2.restriction_axis: the generic group model variant: Maurer (label-free) to Shoup (labelled), with an intermediate rung of Shoup protocols restricted in what they may do with labels
P2.settled_base_case: Maurer's model, every party count at least three, including imperfect correctness (the source's Lemma 19 and Theorem 20)

What must change is that resampling must be made label-consistent, so the eavesdropper resamples inside the fibre of the encoding rather than in the exponent alone.

title: Breaking Fully Quantum Time-Lock Puzzles with Quantum Queries
statement_paraphrase: That a quantum-query extractor with a polynomial query budget and only about n/epsilon rounds recovers the solution of any fully quantum time-lock puzzle in the QROM whose generator makes n queries.

The fully quantum case has no attack.

evidence.claim: The barrier applies to a DIFFERENT statement, and the page has already narrowed past it. Every attack in the source asks only classical queries, and classical-query attacks provably cannot suffice unconditionally: if the paper's asymptotic Quantum Polynomial-Query Simulation Conjecture is false, it builds a fully quantum time-lock puzzle that no classical-query adversary breaks (its Theorem 6.2). The conjecture on the page asks for an attack that itself uses quantum queries, which the barrier does not cover. G1 therefore does not fire, but it fires one step away.

title: Post-Quantum Minimality of One-Way Functions Without a Black-Box Security Reduction
statement_paraphrase: That whenever a classical primitive implies one-way functions classically, its post-quantum security implies post-quantum one-way functions, even when the classical implication is not witnessed by a black-box reduction between the security games.

queries_run: Buxbaum Mahmoody minimality one-way functions post-quantum non-black-box security reduction

evidence.claim: Settled whenever the security implication IS a black-box reduction to a two-message game, for uniform and non-uniform quantum adversaries alike, with the implementation reduction left arbitrary. The source poses the non-black-box case and records it as unresolved: 'Our work leaves open answering our main question when Q implies OWFs through a non-black-box security reduction, or when P uses a more complicated security game than a two-message one'.
evidence.citation: Buxbaum, Mahmoody, A Note on the Minimality of One-Way Functions in Post-Quantum Cryptography, ePrint 2024/2095, IACR Communications in Cryptology

evidence.claim: The page's own caveat is the decisive scoring input: 'Non-black-box security reduction' is not a structured class the way black-box reductions are, and the hypothesis of the conjecture is little more than the bare implication that Q classically exists implies one-way functions classically exist, so a positive proof would have to be a general lifting theorem with no reduction structure to grip. The page's honest reading is that the affirmative direction is not attackable and only the refuting direction has a visible line of attack.
evidence.citation: c/0029 latex/main.tex, caveats for a reviewer

evidence.claim: The surrounding quantum landscape (oracles relative to which pseudorandom states exist while BQP = QMA, and a classical oracle relative to which single-copy pseudorandom states exist while P = NP) is why the question is not obviously affirmative, but no implication makes it a gated barrier.
evidence.citation: Kretschmer 2021; Kretschmer, Qian, Sinha, Tal 2023

evidence.claim: The literature after December 2024 has not been checked for a resolution, which the page itself flags.

P1.justification: The machine-friendly side is the wrong side. The statement is asserted affirmatively, and proving it means a general lifting theorem over an unstructured hypothesis; the only visible line of attack is refutation by a contrived primitive, in the style of the source's own four-message counterexample. Scored at 2 rather than 3 precisely because the constructive side is not the side being asked for, and it yields no partial credit toward the affirmative statement.
P1.construction_side_dual: A contrived classical primitive Q that classically implies one-way functions (necessarily through a non-black-box security reduction) but whose post-quantum security does not imply post-quantum one-way functions. The source's own four-message counterexample, built for the neighbouring axis, is the template. This is the only route with a visible attack and the whole record should be read as a recommendation to attack the dual or nothing.

P2.justification: There is a settled base case and a well-defined neighbouring rung, but they are on the WRONG axis. The settled result is black-box security reduction to a two-message game, and the source names two open directions: more complicated security games (a genuine ladder, three-message then arbitrary), and non-black-box reductions (not a ladder at all, since the class has no structure to climb). This record's target is the second. Minus one for exactly that: the target is not on the axis the base case sits on, and the page records that the source offers no account of what makes the non-black-box case hard and no partial result towards it.
P2.restriction_axis: structure of the security reduction (black-box, then nothing), crossed with the message complexity of the target game (two, then more)
P2.settled_base_case: black-box security reduction to a two-message game: the source's Theorem 1, Theorem 3 and Corollary 1
P2.next_rung: on the productive axis, black-box reduction to a three-message game; on the stated axis, no rung exists
P2.generalization_hypothesis: On the game-complexity axis: the stateful-equivalent-adversary construction survives, answering repeated questions consistently, and only the number of consistency rounds grows. On the stated non-black-box axis: none available, which is the finding.

P3.justification: Capped, and the page's own words are the evidence: a positive proof would have to be a general lifting theorem with no reduction structure to grip. That is a new framework by definition, not a new lemma inside an old one. Composition depth 3 (the source, constructive post-quantum reductions, and the oracle-separation results that make the question live) and a high ambient load (the RTV primitive framework, game-based definitions, QPT versus non-uniform QPT) would hold it near 1 in any case.
P3.candidate_technique: post-quantum lifting of classical reductions; stateful-equivalent adversaries avoiding quantum rewinding. For the dual: contrived-primitive construction in the style of the source's four-message counterexample

title: Asymptotically Optimal Gap Finders for Martingales
statement_paraphrase: That every bounded martingale ending in {0,1} and starting at mu admits an online stopping rule and a threshold whose product of stopping probability and guaranteed jump is Omega(mu / sqrt n), removing the extra factor of mu that the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule loses.

queries_run: Etesami Gao Mahloujifar Mahmoody polynomial-time targeted attacks coin tossing gap finder martingale Cleve Impagliazzo

evidence.claim: Settled when mu is bounded away from zero, where the Cleve-Impagliazzo gap finder already gives the conjectured product; for general mu the known bound is a factor mu short. The source records the two known guarantees side by side in its Theorem 52: a (Omega(mu), Omega(mu/sqrt n)) gap finder from Cleve-Impagliazzo, and an expected-gap bound alpha = 2mu(1-mu)/sqrt(2n-1) from Khorasgani, Maji and Mukherjee. It notes the first was proved for mu = 1/2 and that the same proof carries over to general mu with the stated mu-dependence.
evidence.citation: Etesami, Gao, Mahloujifar, Mahmoody, Polynomial-time targeted attacks on coin tossing for any number of corruptions

evidence.claim: The source poses it in an appendix as an aside: 'This motivates the following question, which as far as we know is open' (p. 45), the question being whether one can always obtain a (rho, alpha) gap finder with rho*alpha = Omega(mu/sqrt n). It takes no position and offers no partial result at intermediate mu.
evidence.citation: same source, p. 45

evidence.claim: The printed question omits the hypothesis that the martingale's final value lies in {0,1}; taken literally it is false, since a martingale constant at mu has no gaps at all. The page restores that hypothesis, which the surrounding text forces. Cleve-Impagliazzo 1993 is an unpublished manuscript, so the base case is available only through the source's restatement.
evidence.citation: c/0030 latex/main.tex, caveats for a reviewer; Cleve and Impagliazzo 1993, unpublished

evidence.claim: No source found closing the small-mu regime.
rungs_tried: arXiv probability search on martingale gap finders

P1.justification: Maximal, and it is the right maximum. The target is an online stopping algorithm together with a threshold: an explicit algorithm, existentially quantified, with no efficiency requirement at all (the page states the bound is information-theoretic and imposes no running-time bound on the rule). That is exactly the object construction search produces, and the conjecture is an existence claim in the same sense as the split-source decomposition anchor.
P1.construction_side_dual: The statement is itself the construction. Its refutation dual is a martingale family on which every online stopping rule has rho*alpha = o(mu/sqrt n); at fixed small n and rational-valued martingales on a finite tree, the optimal rho*alpha is computable exactly by dynamic programming or by an LP over stopping rules, so a counterexample is exactly certifiable and the ratio rho*alpha*sqrt(n)/mu is a scalar to minimise.

P2.justification: One clean axis (mu), a settled base case where the classical rule already meets the target, a well-defined unsettled next rung, and a statable generalization hypothesis. Minus one for the rubric's sharpest warning case: the bound is settled away from the parameter boundary (mu = Theta(1)) and is short by exactly that parameter near it (a factor of mu as mu tends to 0), which is the signature of an ESSENTIAL rather than REMOVABLE use of the restriction. That is the single strongest reason not to treat this as routine.
P2.restriction_axis: the starting value mu of the martingale
P2.settled_base_case: mu = Theta(1), where the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule already gives rho*alpha = Omega(mu/sqrt n)
P2.next_rung: mu = 1/polylog(n), then mu = n^{-c} for a small constant c
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The Cleve-Impagliazzo stopping rule survives as the mechanism; the loss enters through its mu-dependence, since the proof was written for mu = 1/2 and carries over only with a factor mu. The surviving feature is that the rule stops at the first step where the conditional probability moves by a fixed fraction of its current value, and the repair is to make the threshold relative to the current value rather than absolute.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2 (the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule as restated in the source's Theorem 52, plus the Khorasgani-Maji-Mukherjee expected-gap bound), giving a base of 3, and no ambient-load deduction: the page defines martingale, gap finder and online stopping rule self-containedly, with no idealized model and no cryptographic conventions in the object itself. No new framework: this is optimal stopping plus martingale concentration, a standard technique class, and the source already proves a converse showing the target is the right answer if achievable.
P3.candidate_technique: optimal stopping with a relative rather than absolute jump threshold; martingale concentration (Azuma, Freedman); a potential-function or LP-duality argument on the stopping problem

V1.justification: Loses the single-reading point because the source's printed question is FALSE as literally stated: it omits the hypothesis that the martingale's final value lies in {0,1}, without which a martingale constant at mu has no gaps at all. The page restores it, and the surrounding text forces the restoration, so the statement is now determinate; but the record has to note that the target was repaired rather than transcribed. Everything else scores maximally: no idealization; the constant c universally quantified before n, mu and the martingale while alpha and the rule are quantified after it; no adversary and an explicit statement that no running-time bound is imposed; composition not applicable; and a sharp vacuous reading.
V1.idealization: none: finite-horizon discrete martingales, information-theoretic
variants_in_play: the repaired statement, with final value in {0,1} (the subject)
the printed statement without that hypothesis, which is false
the expected-gap formulation of Khorasgani-Maji-Mukherjee, which is a different quantity
V1.vacuous_reading: Read alpha as allowed to depend on the sampled path rather than being fixed before the martingale is sampled: then rho = 1 by construction and the product collapses to a statement about the expected maximal jump, which the Khorasgani-Maji-Mukherjee bound already gives and which answers nothing.

V2.justification: Maximal. At fixed small n the extremal problem is finite: a martingale on a rational-valued tree of depth n with leaves in {0,1} is a finite object, the optimal (rho, alpha) over online stopping rules is computable exactly by dynamic programming or by an LP whose dual gives a certificate, and the quantity rho*alpha*sqrt(n)/mu is an exact rational. So the statement is decidable at named parameters over the enumerated family, not merely probed. Exact rational arithmetic hardens it, with admissibility checks that verify the martingale property, E[w_1] = mu and the terminal condition. And the scalar to minimise is immediate.
V2.finite_instantiation: n <= 6, rational-valued martingale trees with terminal values in {0,1}, mu in a small rational grid; optimal rho*alpha by exact LP or dynamic programming

V3.justification: Lean plus Mathlib is a real match: Mathlib carries conditional expectation, martingales and Doob's theory, and the object here is a finite-horizon discrete martingale with no measure theory over oracle spaces. An LP-dual certificate at small n is a genuine machine-checkable witness. The decomposition point is withheld: the whole difficulty is that the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule loses a factor mu, so finding the rule that does not is the research content and the lemma chain cannot be called cheap to write.

O1.justification: Maximal, and earned on every item. The provenance is exactly the rubric's aside: a question raised in one sentence in an appendix, prefaced 'which as far as we know is open', with no position taken and no partial result offered. Attempt volume is zero. The source is recent and the subarea, quantitative strengthenings of the Cleve-Impagliazzo martingale gap theorem, is as narrow as it gets. Worth recording: this is a thirty-year-old structural theorem being sharpened in the one regime where it is known to be lossy, so it may already be a corollary of something in the optimal-stopping literature, which raises Scout priority without changing attackability.

O2.justification: The source is reachable on ePrint and the expected proof is short: a stopping rule plus its analysis is a few pages as a chain of separately statable lemmas, and the compute is bounded by explicit small-n LPs. One caveat recorded rather than penalised: Cleve-Impagliazzo 1993 is an unpublished manuscript, so the base case is available only through the source's Theorem 52 restatement, which is a single restated step rather than a folklore dependence.
blocked_sources: Cleve and Impagliazzo 1993, unpublished manuscript; available only via the source's Theorem 52 restatement

reasons: R4: the scalar rho*alpha*sqrt(n)/mu is exploitable through martingales that violate the terminal condition, through E[w_1] != mu, through n = 1 degeneracies, and through a rule that chooses alpha after seeing the path (which is also the vacuous reading). Exact rationals plus admissibility checks that raise are the precondition.
R1 not applied: the small-mu regime exists nowhere, and the hazard that a prover recalls the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule is self-detecting, since that rule is exactly the one that is a factor mu short.
R5 not applied: finite martingale and optimal-stopping arguments have a large adjudicating community.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $\mu = n^{-c}$ for a small constant $c$: exhibit an online stopping rule with $\rho \cdot \alpha \ge c'\mu/\sqrt{n}$ in that regime
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: At $n \le 6$ and $\mu$ on a rational grid, compute the exact optimum of $\rho \cdot \alpha \cdot \sqrt{n}/\mu$ over online stopping rules by LP, minimised over martingale trees. Either the optimum stays bounded below by a constant, which says the conjecture is true at small scale and hands the Prover the extremal tree to design against, or it decays with $\mu$, which refutes the conjecture and settles the source's question. Under two pages either way.
configuration.yield_on_failure: An exact table of the achievable constant as a function of $\mu$ and $n$, with an LP-dual certificate. That alone answers whether the missing factor $\mu$ is an artefact of the Cleve-Impagliazzo rule or intrinsic, which is the whole question.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: confirmation that the terminal condition (final value in {0,1}) is intended, since the source's printed question omits it and is false without it
confirmation that alpha must be fixed before the martingale is sampled, not chosen per path

source_requests.identifier: eprint report number as recorded on the page; verify

title: Parity-Only Ring-LWE Is as Hard as Ring-LWE
statement_paraphrase: That an oracle for the error of a Ring-LWE sample modulo two can be turned, with only polynomial loss and only on-distribution queries, into a solver for the full Ring-LWE error.

queries_run: Duman Hovelmanns Kiltz Lyubashevsky Seiler Unruh thorough treatment highly efficient NTRU instantiations error modulo two parity reduction

evidence.claim: The source states plainly that it has no formal reduction for this direction and offers two heuristics instead, on its page 20. Heuristic (i) is iterated stripping: a correct parity answer lets one halve the error and recurse, so the full error is eventually recovered, but each round narrows the error distribution, so the oracle is queried off-distribution and it is not a reduction. Heuristic (ii) is a clean reduction from a NONSTANDARD decision variant in which the first coefficient is noiseless, together with the observation that current algorithms would solve that via its search version.
evidence.citation: Duman, Hovelmanns, Kiltz, Lyubashevsky, Seiler, Unruh, A Thorough Treatment of Highly-Efficient NTRU Instantiations

evidence.claim: The on-distribution clause is not decoration: it is what separates the conjecture from heuristic (i). A reduction that helped itself to the oracle's success on the narrower distributions would be assuming the heuristic rather than proving it. The page makes this explicit and the clause is part of the statement.
evidence.citation: c/0034 latex/main.tex, remark on the on-distribution restriction

evidence.claim: The cited supporting results are the hardness of the First-is-Errorless variant of LWE and a non-tight Module-LWE reduction to a stronger relative; the source concludes only that the concrete hardnesses are equal by assumption, not by proof.
evidence.citation: Brakerski, Langlois, Peikert, Regev, Stehle, STOC 2013; and the Module-LWE reduction cited on the page

evidence.claim: No source found giving the on-distribution reduction. This is the record whose Scout obligation is heaviest: the failure mode is that a standard search-to-decision or bit-recovery reduction for LWE already covers it under another name, and the search run here was keyword-based only.

P1.justification: Maximal, and cleanly so. The target is an oracle algorithm B together with a polynomial P: a reduction, which is an object, existentially quantified before everything else. The source has even written most of it, since heuristic (i) is a working recursion whose only defect is where it queries the oracle. Nothing in the asked-for direction is a lower bound.
P1.construction_side_dual: The statement is itself the construction. Its refutation dual is a separation: a parity oracle, or an oracle world, in which the error modulo two is recoverable but the full error is not, which would show the NTRU instantiation's one-wayness rests on a strictly weaker assumption than Ring-LWE.

P2.justification: An explicit axis with the base case already written by the source, and a next rung that is exactly one step away. Round one of the stripping recursion is on-distribution and therefore sound; round two is not, and that is the entire content. The generalization hypothesis is statable, though it is also where the honest doubt sits. Minus one for the rubric's accident trigger, which applies sharply here: round one works PRECISELY because it is on-distribution, and round two fails precisely because it is not, so the base case's soundness mechanism is exactly what the next rung destroys.
P2.restriction_axis: the number of stripping rounds for which the parity oracle is queried on-distribution
P2.settled_base_case: round one: the first query is on-distribution by hypothesis, so a single parity answer is soundly obtained
P2.next_rung: round two: tolerate one halving of the error, i.e. one off-distribution query
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The stripping recursion survives verbatim; what must be added is a distribution-repair step that re-widens the halved error back to psi_2^d before querying, at a polynomial cost. The named technique is smudging or rejection sampling. The honest doubt, which the Contract should record, is that re-adding noise may destroy the very parities just stripped, in which case the repair is not available and the obstruction is essential rather than removable. That is a two-page question, not a research programme, which is why it is the entry rung.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2 (the source's stripping recursion, and the First-is-Errorless hardness result the second heuristic leans on), giving a base of 3, with no ambient-load deduction: the page defines the error distribution and both advantage notions self-containedly. Not capped, and deliberately so: distribution repair by smudging or rejection sampling is a standard, named technique class in the lattice literature. Weighed against that: three strong lattice authors declined to prove this and published heuristics instead, which is real evidence the naive repair does not go through. The framework's instruction is not to conflate expert difficulty with harness difficulty, and the cheap decidable check at the entry rung is what settles which it is. [Corrected on re-score: the first pass applied a HIGH-load deduction while labelling the load MEDIUM.]
P3.candidate_technique: smudging or rejection sampling to repair distribution drift inside an existing recursion; search-to-decision reductions for Ring-LWE

V1.justification: Maximal, and it is the best-specified statement in the corpus after c/0015 and c/0030. One reading, with the load-bearing clause made explicit as part of the statement rather than left to interpretation: the oracle's guarantee holds only on inputs distributed exactly as in the definition, which is precisely what separates the conjecture from the source's heuristic. No idealization. The quantifier order is written out and the reduction's loss is CONCRETE, a named polynomial in d, log q and 1/epsilon, with an explicit running-time bound. The adversary class is any algorithm with advantage at least epsilon. Composition not applicable. And the vacuous reading is not merely nameable, it is named on the page as the thing the final clause forbids.
V1.idealization: none: standard-model Ring-LWE with an explicitly specified error distribution
variants_in_play: on-distribution queries only (the subject)
off-distribution queries permitted, which is the source's first heuristic and is not a reduction
the first-is-errorless decision variant, which is the source's second heuristic and is a different problem
V1.vacuous_reading: Give a reduction that queries the parity oracle on the narrower distributions produced by later stripping rounds. It looks exactly like a reduction, it terminates, and it assumes the source's heuristic instead of proving it. This is the reading four in five plausible outputs will take.

V2.justification: Maximal, and unusually direct: the quantity that decides the entry rung is itself exactly computable. For d = 6 and q in {7, 11, 13} the error distribution psi_2^d and the round-two distribution after halving are both explicit finite distributions on a small set, so their statistical distance is an exact rational, and the question of whether any polynomial-time re-randomisation bridges them is decidable at those parameters. Exact arithmetic over Z_q hardens it, with admissibility checks that d has the right form, q is a prime above 4, and the oracle's advantage is verified on-distribution rather than assumed. The scalar is the statistical distance, or the reduction's advantage.
V2.finite_instantiation: d = 6, q in {7, 11, 13}: exact rational computation of the statistical distance between psi_2^d and the round-two error distribution, and exhaustive check of candidate re-randomisations

V3.justification: All three. Tool: the object is a game-based reduction over finite rings, which is what EasyCrypt is for, and Mathlib carries the finite-ring and distribution machinery; this is not a QROM or AI-ROM statement, so the rubric's warning does not bite. Decomposition: cheap and known in advance, since the source has already written the recursion and the missing piece is a single distribution-repair lemma plus an induction over rounds, which is textbook shape rather than research content. Witness: the exact small-parameter statistical-distance computation is machine-checkable and settles the entry rung on its own.

title: Soundness of Unruh's Compressed Permutation Oracle
statement_paraphrase: That Unruh's candidate compressed permutation oracle is indistinguishable from a random permutation with forward and inverse access, for EVERY choice of the flipping operator it leaves unspecified.

queries_run: Carolan Compressed Permutation Oracles eprint 2025/1734 STOC 2026 Luby-Rackoff seven round double-sided zero search

evidence.claim: The underlying research question, whether the compressed-oracle technique extends to permutations at all, is now resolved affirmatively by a DIFFERENT construction: Carolan develops and proves sound a compressed permutation oracle whose purification is a small list of input-output pairs, and applies it to show seven-round Feistel is a strong quantum PRP, resolving an open question of Zhandry 2012. Verified: ePrint 2025/1734, arXiv 2509.18586, STOC 2026 (DOI 10.1145/3798129.3800736).
evidence.citation: Carolan, Compressed Permutation Oracles, ePrint 2025/1734, STOC 2026

evidence.claim: Carolan's oracle is, in his own words, similar to Unruh's though he explicitly and unitarily maintains injectivity of the database, which is a change going BEYOND Unruh's own left-open choice of how the flipping operator acts on non-injective inputs. So the statement on this page, which quantifies over every flipping operator, is not settled by his proof on the reading the page defends.
evidence.citation: c/0036 index.qmd, status summary

evidence.claim: The originating construction and its conjectured soundness.
evidence.citation: Unruh, Towards compressed permutation oracles, ePrint 2023/770, ASIACRYPT 2023, pp. 369-400

evidence.claim: Not found: any statement about Unruh's construction with an arbitrary flipping operator, in either direction. The unexamined possibility, and the reason this record recommends a Refuter first, is that a badly chosen flipping operator makes Unruh's oracle UNSOUND, which would explain why Carolan's injectivity maintenance was necessary rather than incidental.
rungs_tried: Carolan's paper abstract and framing as reported

P1.justification: Two-sided, and the machine-friendly side is refutation. The conjecture quantifies over EVERY flipping operator, so a single bad choice with a distinguisher refutes it, and at small domain size that is a finite-dimensional linear-algebra computation. It is a 3 rather than a 4 because the asserted direction is soundness; but a refutation would yield more than partial credit, since it would show Carolan's explicit injectivity maintenance was necessary rather than a matter of taste.
P1.construction_side_dual: A flipping operator Flip on C^{D to D partial} together with a two-query algorithm distinguishing the resulting compressed permutation oracle from a random permutation with inverse access. At |D| = 4 or 8 both the oracle and the ideal object are explicit finite-dimensional unitaries, so the distinguishing advantage is an exact algebraic number and the search over Flip is over a bounded parameter space.

P2.justification: There is now a settled base case that did not exist when the page was written: Carolan's own compressed permutation oracle, with injectivity explicitly maintained, is unconditionally sound. The next rung is Unruh's construction restricted to flipping operators that preserve injectivity on the support, then arbitrary ones. The generalization hypothesis is statable, since Carolan's proof supplies a database invariant to test against a non-injectivity-preserving Flip. Minus one because the base case's mechanism turns on exactly the property the target drops: injectivity is what Carolan's proof maintains and what an arbitrary flipping operator need not respect.
P2.restriction_axis: the class of flipping operators, from injectivity-preserving to arbitrary
P2.settled_base_case: Carolan's construction, which explicitly and unitarily maintains injectivity, unconditionally sound
P2.next_rung: Unruh's construction with the flipping operator restricted to those preserving injectivity on the support
P2.generalization_hypothesis: Carolan's soundness proof rests on a database invariant that survives each query; the surviving feature is that invariant, and the question is exactly whether it can be maintained when the flipping operator is free to act arbitrarily on non-injective inputs. That is testable rather than speculative.

P3.justification: Composition depth 2 (Unruh's construction and Carolan's soundness proof, which supplies the framework), giving a base of 3, minus one for a high ambient convention load: the compressed-oracle formalism over partial functions, the sanitized compressed function oracle, the flipping operator and the treatment of backward queries are all carried context and are exactly where a mis-transcription would land. Not capped: Carolan has supplied the framework, so what remains is applying and stressing it rather than inventing one.
P3.candidate_technique: compressed oracle with a database invariant; explicit small-dimension unitary computation for the refutation side

V1.justification: Loses the single-reading point for a live and consequential reason: whether Carolan's theorem settles this depends on a reading, and the repo's own status text says 'on the reading defended here' it does not. That is precisely the situation where a correct proof of the wrong statement passes every local check. Everything else scores: the idealization is named and the sibling QROM compressed-FUNCTION oracle is distinguished; the quantifiers are pinned explicitly (for every polynomial p there is a negligible mu, for every D, every Flip, every algorithm with at most p(log|D|) queries); the adversary class is a query-bounded but otherwise unbounded oracle algorithm; composition is not applicable; and the vacuous reading is sharp.
V1.idealization: quantum random permutation with forward and inverse access; compressed permutation oracle
variants_in_play: Unruh's construction with an arbitrary flipping operator (the subject)
Carolan's construction with injectivity explicitly maintained (a theorem)
the compressed FUNCTION oracle, where the technique is standard
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove soundness only for the flipping operator that maintains injectivity, which is Carolan's construction and is already a theorem. The 'for every Flip' quantifier is the entire remaining content, and dropping it turns an open problem into a restatement of published work.

V2.justification: Maximal, and it is the reason to buy a Refuter here rather than a Prover. At |D| = 4 or 8 the compressed permutation oracle and the ideal forward-plus-inverse permutation oracle are both explicit unitaries on a finite-dimensional space, so the distinguishing advantage of any two-query algorithm is an exact algebraic quantity computable by linear algebra, and the space of flipping operators is a bounded parameter space to search. Exact rational or algebraic arithmetic hardens it, with admissibility checks that Flip is unitary and the oracle well-defined. The scalar is the distinguishing advantage.
V2.finite_instantiation: |D| in {4, 8}, query count at most 2, exact algebraic linear algebra over explicit unitaries, search over the flipping operator's parameters

V3.justification: The tool point is withheld: the statement is asymptotic in |D| over quantum oracle algorithms, which no listed assistant covers well, and the rubric's warning about scoring Lean alone for quantum oracle statements applies. The decomposition point IS earned, because Carolan's proof supplies the invariant and hence the lemma chain a human would write. And a small-dimension counterexample certificate or exact computation is a real witness.

O1.justification: No provenance bonus: Unruh states the soundness of his construction as a conjecture in a paper whose title is 'Towards' it. Attempt volume is low but nonzero, since Carolan attacked the underlying question and went around this cell. Recent source and narrow subarea. Recorded separately, and it is the most important thing about this record: the statement is plausibly a corollary, or a refuted corollary, of Carolan's analysis that nobody has connected, and the payoff of settling it has largely collapsed now that the research question it existed to serve is answered.

O2.justification: Both sources reachable (ePrint 2023/770 and 2025/1734, plus an arXiv version), no folklore step, compute bounded by explicit small dimensions, and a short expected shape: a counterexample flipping operator with its distinguisher is a couple of pages, and so is a soundness proof restricted to injectivity-preserving operators once Carolan's invariant is in hand.

reasons: R1: Carolan's paper is pre-cutoff and in training data, and the failure mode is exactly the reading ambiguity that costs V1 its first point: recall his soundness theorem and present it as a proof of Unruh's conjecture. That would look like a success and would be a correct proof of a different statement.
R4: the distinguishing-advantage scalar is exploitable through non-unitary flipping operators, ill-defined oracles, and query-count violations.
R5: compressed permutation oracles are the working vocabulary of about five people.

Either a counterexample, which refutes the conjecture and explains why Carolan's injectivity maintenance is necessary, or a certificate that no flipping operator distinguishes at that size, which is evidence for soundness and identifies the invariant. definitions_needing_repair: The one-shot-decryption security experiment has two inequivalent readings and the page does not resolve them. As PRINTED (the source's Experiment 2, p. 19) an exempt party's state is handed to the adversary nowhere at all; the source's PROSE (p. 17) says the adversary 'can corrupt all parties after decryption'. On the prose reading, corrupting a party after it has partially decrypted is free and delivers its state, which is a materially stronger requirement. Which reading is intended decides what one-shot decryption means and therefore what has to be built.

The one-shot signature definition needed a repair to be satisfiable at all: the clause m_0 != m_1 is not printed in the source's Definition 5 (p. 12), and without it the requirement is unsatisfiable, since honest key generation followed by signing already yields two verifying pairs. The page adds it as clearly intended, matching the AGKZ20 definition. That repair is almost certainly right, but it is a repair, and the message space is left as an abstract set whose relation to the source's own Algorithm 1 is also flagged.

The hypotheses themselves. The source's question is disjunctive (weaken the assumption, restrict it, or find an alternative realization), and the page's clauses (i) and (ii) pick one branch. Which branch is the target has to be a human decision, because the three branches are three different problems and only one of them is a construction from named primitives.

title: A Dream Direct Product Theorem for a Moderately Hard Function
statement_paraphrase: That some moderately hard function family amplifies its per-instance success bound to exactly its t-th power over t independent instances, with no loss in the exponent.

It establishes three things about what is needed: the required soundness must satisfy epsilon <= 2^{-Omega(d)} because the sampler's hardness-preservation loss is 2^{Omega(d)}; complexity leveraging cannot supply it, since raising the puzzle's security parameter in proportion to d raises honest solving time in proportion to d; and existing proofs of work from fine-grained hardness assumptions fall short of subexponential soundness.

evidence.claim: The source mentions NSETH exactly once, on its page 23, without defining it and without citing anything for it, and its reference list contains no Carmosino et al. entry. It writes 'assuming, say, NSETH', so NSETH is its example rather than its commitment.

definitions_needing_repair: The definition of moderate hardness. The page states that its Definition of moderate hardness is the record's ADAPTATION of the source's Definition 14 and departs from it in three ways, all of them the record's own choices rather than the paper's, including an oracle restriction clause ('none of which lies in {z_1,...,z_t}') that does not appear in the source at all. The conjecture is a statement about that definition, so three unratified departures make it three possible statements.

The hardness hypothesis. The source writes 'assuming, say, NSETH', so NSETH is an example rather than a commitment, and the page supplies both the NSETH definition and its customary reference from the standard literature rather than from the source. The page then says outright that a solver should feel free to substitute another standard fine-grained hypothesis. When the hypothesis is up to the solver, choosing it is part of the task, which is what this gate is for.

The relation between the evaluation cost r, the parameter beta, and the instance count. The page records that it constrains neither r nor beta beyond their types, matching the source, and lists two further side conditions it considered and did not impose. Whether the intended statement is the unconstrained one matters, because an unconstrained r admits families whose evaluation cost makes the amplification claim empty.
