title: The STB Conjecture for Short Merkle-Damgard Collisions
statement_paraphrase: That the auxiliary-input advantage of finding a B-block collision in salted Merkle-Damgard hashing is exactly Theta((STB + T^2)/N) for every B between 2 and T.

queries_run: Akshima Cash Drucker Wee time-space tradeoffs short collisions Merkle-Damgard STB conjecture Akshima Guo Liu

evidence.claim: Open for non-constant B in the regime ST^2 > 2^n, where the best published bound and the best published attack are a factor of up to S apart; settled at B=1, B=2, every constant B, B about T, and every 2 < B < T with ST^2 <= 2^n.
evidence.citation: Akshima, Cash, Drucker, Wee, Time-Space Tradeoffs and Short Collisions in Merkle-Damgard Hash Functions, CRYPTO 2020; Akshima, Guo, Liu, CRYPTO 2022

evidence.claim: Two technique barriers are proved, and they are why P3 is capped. The source's Theorem 5 gives a bit-fixing adversary finding length-2 collisions with advantage Omega(PT/N), so the bit-fixing model is blind to collision length and no bound proved there transfers. Its Theorem 8 settles the conjecture's upper bound against the whole class of zero-walk adversaries, up to a factor ln(NB), for B <= T and SB >= T, which is the shape of every attack currently known, so a refutation cannot come from that class either. The two published routes past the barrier, compression with a modified Impagliazzo-Kabanets argument and average-case presampling via high-knowledge-gaining events, both stall at exactly the open regime. Note on gates: the barriers recorded for this record are TECHNIQUE barriers (a named method provably cannot reach the target), not framework barriers. G1 covers relativization, natural proofs, algebrization, black-box separations, meta-reductions, and transferred open problems, none of which applies, and no source claims that a proof would resolve a named open problem elsewhere. The cost of the technique barrier is therefore charged to P3's hard cap, not to a gate.
evidence.citation: c/0050 latex/main.tex, what a resolution must not assume; c/0050 index.qmd difficulty note

evidence.claim: Two transcription issues are recorded on the page and both bear on the statement. The range 2 <= B <= T is supplied by the page; the source prints the claim with no range attached. And read literally the bare Theta is not established even by the source's own attack, whose Theorem delivers Omega((STB - 96S)/(N log N)), short of Omega(STB/N) by a log factor; every subsequent treatment of the conjecture reads the Theta up to logarithmic factors.
evidence.citation: c/0050 latex/main.tex, the range of B; whether the Theta is meant up to logarithmic factors

evidence.claim: No source found closing the non-constant-B regime.
rungs_tried: citing-papers scan of CRYPTO 2020 and CRYPTO 2022
the ITC 2024 multicollision paper, read for adjacent results

P1.justification: Scored between the rubric's 1 and 2, and the reasoning is worth stating because it recurs across this cluster. In form this is tight-bound closure, which would be a 2: the attack exists and only the matching bound is missing. But the constructive side is already PUBLISHED, so it offers no partial credit toward what remains, and what remains is a security bound in the auxiliary-input random oracle model, that is, a lower bound against unbounded offline preprocessing with S bits of non-uniform advice, which is the rubric's 0. The net is 1.
P1.construction_side_dual: An attack finding B-block collisions with advantage asymptotically above STB/N + T^2/N for non-constant B in the regime ST^2 > 2^n. The source's Theorem 8 rules out every zero-walk attack, which is the shape of all known attacks, so the dual has to leave that class: the Refuter's target is an attack whose online phase does not walk to a precomputed collision.

P2.justification: Many settled cells, a well-defined next rung, and a narrow gap, but no generalization hypothesis: the two published routes provably stall at exactly this regime and the bit-fixing model is proved blind to collision length, so no feature of any settled proof is expected to survive. Minus one for the rubric's explicit warning case, which fits exactly: the bound is settled away from the parameter boundary (ST^2 <= 2^n) and is short by a factor of up to S near it. That is the signature of an essential rather than removable use of the restriction.
P2.restriction_axis: the block bound B, crossed with the regime boundary ST^2 versus 2^n
P2.settled_base_case: B=1, B=2, every constant B, B about T, and every 2 < B < T with ST^2 <= 2^n
P2.next_rung: B = log n in the regime ST^2 > 2^n
P2.generalization_hypothesis: None available, and the absence is documented rather than inferred: the source proves the bit-fixing model cannot see collision length, and both published routes (compression with a modified Impagliazzo-Kabanets argument, and average-case presampling via high-knowledge-gaining events) stall at precisely the open regime.

P3.justification: Capped, on two proved technique barriers rather than on judgement. Composition depth 3 or more (the presampling framework, the compression route, the high-knowledge-gaining-event route) and a high ambient convention load would put it near 1 anyway.
P3.candidate_technique: compression and presampling; high-knowledge-gaining event decomposition; multi-instance reductions. All three are proved insufficient in this regime by the sources themselves.

V1.justification: Loses two points. Single reading: the bare Theta as printed is not established even by the source's own attack, and the literature reads it up to logarithmic factors, so two readings are live and one of them is currently unproved in BOTH directions. Pinned quantifiers: the implicit constants and the logarithmic convention inside the Theta are precisely what is unpinned, and the range of B is supplied by the page rather than the source. It earns the rest: the idealization named unambiguously (auxiliary-input random oracle, salted Merkle-Damgard, with the bit-fixing and presampling variants explicitly distinguished); the adversary class fully specified as S bits of advice, T online queries, a fresh random salt and B-block messages; composition not applicable; and a sharp vacuous reading.

variants_in_play: bare Theta (as printed) versus Theta up to polylog factors (as the literature reads it)
auxiliary-input versus bit-fixing/presampling versus multi-instance models
the sibling c/0053, which is the same question with a quantum adversary, and c/0051, which is the sponge analogue
V1.vacuous_reading: Prove the upper half only in the regime ST^2 <= 2^n, which is already settled; or read the Theta up to logarithmic factors and prove only the lower half, which the source's own attack nearly gives and which is not where the difficulty is.

V2.justification: Maximal, and it is the whole reason to spend anything here rather than parking it. The auxiliary-input advantage is not exactly computable at small N, but the BIT-FIXING instantiation is: with the advice a set of at most P fixed input-output pairs, the advantage of a given adversary is an exact rational at N = 16 or 64, and the source's own Theorem 5 bit-fixing adversary is explicit and can be evaluated exactly. That gives a decidable finite instantiation of the question that actually carries the barrier. Exact rationals harden it, with admissibility checks on the advice length, the query count, the block budget and salt freshness. The scalar is the advantage times N/(STB).
V2.finite_instantiation: P-bit-fixing model at N in {16, 64}, S and T small, B in {2,3,4}: exact rational advantage computation, including the source's explicit Theorem 5 adversary

V3.justification: No tool match: the rubric says outright that measure-theoretic probability over oracle spaces plus asymptotics is thinly covered, which is exactly what an AI-ROM bound is. The decomposition is the research content, and both published routes stall. The one point is for a witness: an exact bit-fixing-model computation, or an explicit attack with an exactly computed advantage.

O1.justification: Zero, and it is the honest floor. This is a named conjecture with a tradition: the STB conjecture, carried through CRYPTO 2020, CRYPTO 2022, Ghoshal-Komargodski, Freitag-Ghoshal-Komargodski and the TCC 2023 sponge line, with several papers citing it AS an open problem and attempting it. No obscurity dividend and no recency dividend.

O2.justification: Sources reachable in CRYPTO proceedings and on ePrint, no folklore step, and the small-parameter compute is bounded. But these are paper-length compression and presampling developments whose error accounting is not separable into independently statable lemmas.

reasons: R1: heavily worked and pre-cutoff, with many settled cells in training data. A produced argument is at high risk of being one of those cells restated, so any output must be re-scouted on technique rather than on statement.
R4: the advantage predicate is exploitable through block-budget violations, miscounted advice length, a salt that is not fresh, and bit-fixing advice that exceeds P.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: $B = 3$ in the regime $ST^{2} > 2^{n}$, bit-fixing model first: what is the exact maximum advantage of a $P$-bit-fixing adversary at small $N$, and does it exceed $STB/N$?

Either the computation reproduces the barrier, confirming that bit-fixing is blind to $B$ at small scale, or it does not, which would be a genuine surprise about the source's own theorem. Under two pages.

Buy this, and do not buy a Prover wave: with $P = 4$, $V = 8$ and $O = 2$ the expected value of a proof attempt here is low, and the verdict is a PROBE only because the cheap exact refutation is worth having.

the intended range of B, which the source's printed sentence does not attach

title: The Sponge STB Conjecture
statement_paraphrase: That the auxiliary-input advantage of finding a B-block collision in sponge hashing is Otilde(STB/C + T^2/min(R,C)) for every B at least two.

queries_run: Akshima Duan Guo Liu time-space lower bounds short collisions sponge hash functions TCC 2023 multi-instance

evidence.claim: Open for every B >= 2 except B about T: at B=2 in the regime ST^3 > C, and at B >= 3 with a gap of about T/B. The source asks for a proof or a refutation and takes no position.
evidence.citation: Akshima, Duan, Guo, Liu, On Time-Space Lower Bounds for Finding Short Collisions in Sponge Hash Functions, TCC 2023

evidence.claim: The technique barrier is proved and is why P3 is capped. The source's Theorem 3 exhibits multi-instance adversaries of advantage (S^2T^4/C^2)^S at B=2 and (ST^2/C)^S at B >= 3, so routing a bound through the multi-instance reduction cannot beat S^2T^4/C^2 at two blocks nor ST^2/C at three or more. The paper says outright that 'other novel techniques are required', and the one substitute it names, stateless multi-instance games, is itself unanalyzed. title: Full Composability Implies Circular Security
statement_paraphrase: That the existence of a fully composable homomorphic encryption scheme implies the existence of a circular secure encryption scheme, constructed from it.

queries_run: Micciancio fully composable homomorphic encryption circular security bootstrapping Communications in Cryptology

evidence.claim: Open with no partial result in either direction. The converse, that circular security plus limited homomorphism gives full composability, is the source's Theorem 6; this direction is conjectured there in one English sentence and nothing has been published towards it.
evidence.citation: Micciancio, Fully Composable Homomorphic Encryption, ePrint 2024/1545; IACR Communications in Cryptology 2(1), 2025

evidence.claim: Both directions are recorded as out of reach, and the reasons are different. For the affirmative: nothing in the literature builds a circular-secure scheme out of a homomorphic one, the known technology runs the other way, and the obvious weakening (that a composable scheme is ALREADY circular secure) is refuted by adapting the standard counterexamples, so a resolution has to construct a genuinely different scheme. For the refutation: it would need an oracle world containing fully composable homomorphic encryption and no circular-secure encryption at all, and the black-box separation machinery has never been aimed at a primitive as strong as composable FHE.
evidence.citation: c/0054 index.qmd difficulty note

evidence.claim: The decisive scoring input is on the page itself: circular secure encryption is known to exist under concrete assumptions such as LWE, so in the world we believe we live in the conclusion of the formalized conjecture holds outright. The content of the conjecture is therefore purely the implication in the oracle-world sense, that no world contains fully composable homomorphic encryption without circular-secure encryption. That makes the actual target a black-box separation question, which is the least machine-friendly object in the corpus.
evidence.citation: c/0054 latex/main.tex, why the formalization is not vacuous

evidence.claim: Three readings are the page's rather than the source's, which states only one English sentence and does not say what 'modified into' quantifies over: that the conclusion is the existence of a circular secure scheme rather than a property of the original, that the encoding is existentially rather than universally quantified, and one further choice. The page also records that the source measures IND-CPA advantage as (beta - betabar)^2/(beta + betabar) following Micciancio-Walter bit security, which for adversaries that always output a bit is the SQUARE of the usual distinguishing gap.
evidence.citation: c/0054 latex/main.tex, remarks on the reading and on the advantage convention

P1.justification: The lowest directionality score among the ungated records, and the page earns it for us: because circular secure encryption is known to exist under LWE, the formalized statement's conclusion already holds in the real world, so its entire content is the oracle-world implication. The target is therefore a black-box separation-style claim quantified over worlds, not a construction, even though it is dressed as one. There is no machine-friendly side at all.
P1.construction_side_dual: A generic construction taking any valid, IND-CPA secure, fully composable homomorphic scheme and producing a circular secure one. This is what a proof would have to exhibit, and it is worth recording that no construction in the circular-security literature takes a homomorphic scheme as input, so the dual is empty of precedent. On the other side, a refutation needs an oracle world with composable homomorphic encryption and no circular-secure encryption, which the separation machinery has never been aimed at.

P2.justification: Almost nothing. There is no settled base case on this axis: the source's Theorem 6 is the CONVERSE direction, which is a different statement, and the obvious weakening is refuted rather than proved. A next rung is namable (composability plus some additional property implies circular security), which earns the single point, but no generalization hypothesis is available because there is no base-case proof to generalize, and the gap is not narrow because nothing marks its width.

P2.generalization_hypothesis: None available. The known technology runs the other way, from circular security to composability, and no construction in the circular-security literature takes a homomorphic scheme as input.

P3.justification: Capped. Both directions require machinery that does not exist: a generic construction of a circular-secure scheme from a homomorphic one, of which there is no precedent, or a black-box separation aimed at a primitive as strong as composable FHE, which has never been attempted. Composition depth 1 in its favour, ambient load high (fully composable homomorphic encryption, circular security with encodings, and an advantage convention that is the square of the usual gap).

title: A Safe Two-Scheme Key Cycle for Every Encryption Scheme
statement_paraphrase: That for every IND-CPA secure public-key encryption scheme there is a second scheme such that the two-step key cycle between them can be published without harming the first.

queries_run: Micciancio fully composable homomorphic encryption key cycle two scheme circular security counterexample partner chosen after

evidence.claim: Open in both directions, and the source says why the existing separations miss it: the counterexamples fix both schemes, whereas here the second is chosen AFTER the first. The partner is not required to be homomorphic or to be good for anything else.
evidence.citation: Micciancio, Fully Composable Homomorphic Encryption, ePrint 2024/1545; IACR Communications in Cryptology 2(1), 2025

evidence.claim: Both directions are recorded as hard for stated reasons. Refuting it needs a single scheme poisoned against every possible partner, which no known technique produces: the standard constructions embed an obfuscated or LWE-based trigger that fires on a ciphertext of a specific shape, and the partner is free to avoid that shape. Proving it needs a generic construction of a cooperating partner from an arbitrary scheme, and the only handle the hypothesis offers is IND-CPA security, from which circular security is not known to follow.
evidence.citation: c/0055 index.qmd difficulty note

evidence.claim: The two implicit hypotheses have been supplied and are documented, so the statement is now determinate. The page's own degenerate-reading remark identifies the first: the printed conjecture is trivially true if the partner may be an arbitrary triple of algorithms without the validity requirement, since a partner whose encryption outputs a constant carries no information about the secret key while the other half of the cycle encrypts an independent random string. The second is that the first scheme must be assumed IND-CPA secure, without which the conclusion is false for trivial reasons. The page also records that the source measures IND-CPA advantage following Micciancio-Walter bit security, which for adversaries that always output a bit is the SQUARE of the usual distinguishing gap.
evidence.citation: c/0055 latex/main.tex, a degenerate reading to exclude; two more choices made here; the source's advantage convention

evidence.claim: No source found in either direction. The page presents both the conjecture as printed and one formalization, so the record is about the formalization.

P1.justification: Two-sided, with a constructive side that is the side being asked for. The target is a second scheme built from the first, plus injective encodings: objects. What holds it below maximal is the universal quantification over the first scheme, together with the fact that the only handle the hypothesis offers is IND-CPA security, from which circular security is not known to follow. Note that unusually BOTH directions here are constructions, since a refutation is a single poisoned scheme rather than a separation.
P1.construction_side_dual: A single IND-CPA secure scheme poisoned against every possible partner: one for which no valid second scheme makes the two-step cycle safe. The page records why no known technique produces it, since the standard counterexamples embed a trigger that fires on ciphertexts of a specific shape and a partner chosen afterwards is free to avoid that shape. That observation is itself the design constraint a Refuter would work against.

P2.justification: Nearly empty, and this is what parks the record's proof prospects. There is no settled base case: the whole circular-security counterexample literature has the OPPOSITE quantifier shape, exhibiting particular schemes or particular pairs whose cycle is insecure, and none of it constrains a partner chosen after the fact to cooperate. A next rung is namable, which earns the single point, but with no base-case proof there is no generalization hypothesis, and nothing marks the width of the gap.
P2.restriction_axis: the class of first schemes for which a partner must be found
P2.settled_base_case: none. The existing counterexamples fix both schemes and so do not bear on this quantifier order.
P2.next_rung: restrict the first scheme to a structured class, for instance schemes that are already homomorphic, or LWE-based schemes, and construct the partner there
P2.generalization_hypothesis: None available: no construction in the circular-security literature takes an arbitrary IND-CPA scheme as input and produces a cooperating partner.

P3.justification: Capped. Proving it needs a generic construction of a cooperating partner from an arbitrary scheme and the only handle is IND-CPA security, from which circular security is not known to follow; that is a new framework, not a new lemma. Composition depth 1 in its favour, and a high ambient load: the cycle-scheme definition, the injective encodings, and an advantage convention that is the square of the usual distinguishing gap.
P3.candidate_technique: none identified for the affirmative direction. For the refutation, the obfuscation-based and LWE-based trigger constructions are the precedent, and the page explains why they do not reach the required quantifier order.

V1.justification: Loses only the single-reading point, and for a documented reason rather than a defect: the page carries both the conjecture as printed and one formalization, so two statements are on the table. Everything else scores, and the negative-control item scores emphatically because the page has already done the work: it states the degenerate reading explicitly and excludes it, and it supplies the two hypotheses without which the statement is not non-vacuous. It also pins the advantage convention, which is the square of the usual gap and would otherwise silently change every quantitative claim.
V1.idealization: none: standard-model public-key encryption
variants_in_play: the conjecture as printed versus the page's formalization
whether the partner must be IND-CPA secure or merely valid
the Micciancio-Walter squared advantage convention versus the usual distinguishing gap
V1.vacuous_reading: Take the partner to be an arbitrary triple of algorithms without the validity requirement, its encryption outputting a constant: then the partner's ciphertext of the secret key carries no information, the other half of the cycle encrypts an independent random string, and IND-CPA security of the first scheme finishes it. The page names this reading and excludes it, which is exactly why the validity requirement is load-bearing.

V2.justification: Zero. A computational statement quantified over all IND-CPA secure schemes has no finite instantiation, nothing to harden and no scalar: whether a candidate partner makes the cycle safe is a proof obligation, not a computable quantity. This is the axis that keeps the record out of the campaign set despite an unusually good obscurity dividend.
V2.finite_instantiation: none

V3.justification: The tool point is available: the cycle scheme's IND-CPA game is pseudocodable and SSProve or EasyCrypt model this kind of game hopping directly. Nothing else: a generic partner construction is the research content, and there is no witness short of a full proof.

O1.justification: Maximal. The provenance is an aside in the purest form: one sentence in a paper whose results lie elsewhere, never returned to, and the page had to supply two hypotheses to make it a statement at all. Attempt volume is zero. The source is recent (2024 ePrint, 2025 journal) and the setting is narrow.

O2.justification: Reachable source, no folklore step, no solver call. But a generic construction of a cooperating partner from an arbitrary scheme, or a scheme poisoned against every partner, is a paper-length development with no natural short lemma chain.

reasons: R5: this sits inside one author's framework and turns on a quantifier order that the surrounding counterexample literature does not address, so the pool able to adjudicate a claimed resolution is small.
R1 not applied: nothing exists in either direction. R4 not applied because there is no predicate, which is the same fact that zeroes V2.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: Restrict the first scheme to a structured class: for every IND-CPA secure scheme whose ciphertexts are linearly homomorphic, construct a valid partner making the two-step cycle safe
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Take the standard circular-security counterexample constructions, whose trigger fires on ciphertexts of a specific shape, and determine whether a partner can be built to avoid that shape systematically rather than by luck. Either a generic avoidance construction for a structured class, or a demonstration that the trigger can be made shape-oblivious, which would be the first step towards a poisoned scheme. Two pages.
configuration.yield_on_failure: A characterisation of what a circular-security trigger can and cannot detect about a partner chosen after the fact, which is the reusable ingredient for both directions and is worth writing up alone. This is the honest expected best output, and the campaign should be scoped to it rather than to the full statement.
